title: Captions of the four Public videos: rebuild with the kit's orphan fix (7/15/23/16 orphan tails live on YouTube), replace the caption tracks on the owner's word
description:
## Why

The four Public videos' English caption tracks on YouTube were built before the kit's captions fix (1f44182: a sentence that needs several cues is split at the word breaks that maximize the shortest, instead of leaving its last word or two alone on a brief cue). `./x SLUG release-check` (tools/release.py, which since d7ece6c fails such an orphan tail) finds on the laptop copies of the uploaded SRTs: Hoeffding michael 7, fish michael v4 15, RaptorQ michael 23, bakery michael 16. An orphan is a cue like 'better.' for 0.43 s: too brief to read, the end of a sentence flashing alone. Viewers who use captions see them in all four.

## What

1. For each of the four, rebuild the captions from the same narration report and the same final timelines with the kit at or after 1f44182, without touching the render (as done for E: `BIN captions --narration NARRATION_OUT --out SCRATCH_DIR_WITH_COPIES_OF_THE_FINAL_TIMELINES`; the narration and timelines live where each final was rendered; find them from MANIFEST's paths and the cut's commit).
2. Check each: the same words in the same order as the uploaded SRT (diff of the joined cue texts), at most 2 lines of 42 characters, no orphan tail (release-check on a copy with the new SRT), every cue inside the master.
3. Owner's call (through GreenCarp/BronzeRidge): replace the caption track of each Public video in YouTube Studio with the rebuilt SRT (no re-upload of the video, no new link). Record in MANIFEST the new SRT md5 and date, the old SRT kept beside it.

## Done when

Each Public video's live caption track is the rebuilt SRT (BronzeRidge confirms from Studio), MANIFEST records its md5, and release-check finds no orphan tail in any of the four. If the owner declines, record that and close.

title: Score: the theme tunes of F, K and J are moved by rule 7 (title motif and closing resolution not as written); Identity::theme_chord
description:
Rule 7 (score::avoid_minor_ninths) moves a melody note that is a semitone from any chord tone. It does this to the identity's own theme too, so three videos' leitmotifs do not sound as written (found by scoring each E-K video's current timelines at HEAD and reading the Melody events in their theme gaps; CloudyFinch, 2026-10-14):

- F mental_math: title motif D E F# A plays E E F# A (D is a semitone from C# in Dmaj9 and Bm9); the closing resolution F# E D ends E E: the video never lands on the tonic. F's final (e1b0ad3) has this.
- K eigen_engineering: title motif E B E G# plays E B E F# (G# next to A in Amaj9 / B7sus4); the closing resolution B G# E ends B G# F#: no tonic.
- J matrix_exponential: title motif A B B C C E plays A B B B B E (the tune's own half step B-C clashes with Am9/Cmaj9, which hold both); the last gap's resolution D C B A plays D D A A.
- E, G, H, I: as written (G fixed in 8913e27 by changing its chords; I designed against it).

Fix: Identity::theme_chord (None for every video by default, so nothing else moves): the bed's chord under a theme's phrase (the gap of a soundless listen window the identity themes, and the video's last gap when it resolves), chosen by the video so its tune clears it. F D6/9, K E6/9, J A7sus4. Tests: engine render test (tune as written over the theme chord, moved without it), per-video test that every tune pitch clears its theme chord, real timelines re-scored.
close_reason: Landed in 0720552; F, K, J theme chords verified, mental_math v2 verified exit 0 at 14:15:30 UTC

title: Narration: join-aware read choice (DP over each line) with --seed candidates (choose)
description: Research RS-20261014-narration (laptop ~/brennerbot_sessions): the median sentence-join reset is human (+7-9 st) but F has 29-31% of joins beyond +12 st vs human 7-12%, from deeper endings (T-007, audits). T-003: a join-aware pick among the existing reads cuts joins beyond +-7 st 29%->12%. Audit A D7: ftts --seed 1..7 gives different reads, deterministic per seed (N-10/INFRA.md:287 wrong). Build in tools/narration.py choose (portable to the skill's narrate.py): candidates = quote wrappers + --seed 1..N that pass the existing gates; DP over the line with node cost (existing score + stalls over 0.45 s, extra onset syllable, terminal events, statement-final rise) and join cost (reset beyond +12 st, register step) from a consensus of 2 trackers. Tests on synthetic candidates (no ftts): DP finds the optimum; a planted bad join is avoided; no picks => byte-identical to today's choice.
close_reason: Landed in 5933b2f + ca2bc83 (GentleDog, from MaroonMarsh's P-2 DP), opt-in per run (SEEDS=N JOINT=1 [JOINT_CREAK=W] ./x <slug> narrate). Independent review by SunnyMarsh (bead comment 08:03 UTC): choose without --joint byte-identical to the old choose on real data (P-2's ch02 work dir: 12 files; Video E's whole narration: 65 files); the planted bad join and the assembled-line re-gate verified on P-2's real lost-'But' case; effect on ch02 joins past +12 st 4 -> 0 (two Praat-class trackers), 4 -> 2 (pyin); out of sample on Video E smaller (21 -> 18). Findings H1 (final s/z regression 0 -> 2 on Video E), M1 (creak on by default), M2 (lost-first-word path untested), M4 (exclusions not keyed to the script) fixed in ca2bc83 and re-checked by SunnyMarsh (08:35 UTC): all fixed, holding on real data and against mutants. Tests: tools/test_narration_joint.py + test_driver.py green. Not decided here: whether a video turns JOINT on (the owner's A/B).

comments.author: MaroonMarsh
comments.text: P-2 pilot evidence for this bead (no repo edits; scratch scripts on the build host in ~/jmev_orch/narr_exp/P-2/ and P-2/ch07/, copies + numbers in the Brenner workspace evidence/P-2.md): DP over each line (Viterbi; node = score + gates + creak<80 Hz + rising-statement; join = reset beyond +12 st), candidates = the planner's reads plus one straight-quoted input per sentence (finisher makes 5 reads/sentence), assembled by the unchanged production choose with NARRATION_PICKS naming every sentence. F ch 02: joins beyond +12 st 3->0 of 12, creaky endings 17->11 of 21, hesitations 3->0, 16 of 21 sentences changed; F ch 07: beyond +12 11->3 of 22 (median +12.1->+8.2), creaky 21->17 of 29, cut-short reads 8->1, 21 of 29 changed. choose with the current picks reproduces production out/*.wav sample for sample (ch 02 9/9, ch 07 7/7). Needed for the tool: (1) measure each read AFTER nar.edit (the assembled sentence), not the raw span; (2) a line-level gate loop after choose: asr_batch on the lines, qa_lines + narration.py edges + validate, then exclude the failing sentence's chosen tag (cost +5) and rerun the DP: ch 02 lost the first word 'But' in the line transcript with a read whose take-level ASR had it, ch 07 lost the last word 'nine' of 07_5.1; (3) a statement ending on a rise of more than 8 st must be a gate, not a weight (07_5.4 got +16.3 st otherwise because the other reads were cut short); (4) asr_batch --known writes only new transcripts: merge before analyze/choose; (5) a reads.tsv extra input yields 4 new reads (finisher wraps it and wraps the curly read again). Not heard by anyone yet: the owner A/B page (GoldenMountain) is for that; held-out pitch trackers agree on the tail but disagree by 5-20 st on creaky joins.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
mx-4kc2 landed at 5933b2f (tools/narration.py, tools/test_narration_joint.py, tools/test_driver.py, x), pushed to main. Opt-in: nothing changes unless a run sets JOINT=1 (choose) or SEEDS=N (plan + synth).

WHAT IT DOES
- `choose --joint`: Viterbi over each line (MaroonMarsh's P-2, same weights). Node cost = 2*(1-score) + 5 per gate (cut_short, final s/z, asr_ratio<0.85) + names/hesitations/stalls + [ours] hole (unlicensed pause >0.45 s) 1.0, heard word before the first scripted one 1.0 (leading "and" ignored), statement rise 0.25/st, creaky ending 1.0 (P-2's definition), terminal pitch event 2.0; join cost = reset past +12 st (1.0 + 0.2/st) + [ours] register step past 4 st at 0.1/st. A director's pick is forced; ties go to narrate.py's read (+0.02 on any other). Reads moved off narrate.py's pick carry `joint` {from, node, join} in report.json; with --joint off, analyze() keeps the report's key order, so a run is byte for byte the old one (tested).
- `plan --seeds N`: every planned read again with `ftts --seed 1..N`, tags content-addressed (`<id>__s<j>__<hash of base tag + seed>`), listed in work/seeds.tsv and NOT takes.tsv (tts_batch.py would synthesize them without the seed under a seeded tag). `synth WORK` makes them through tts_batch.py's own batch (resumable, serial retries) with `--seed`.
- `exclude`: after the line-level gates (qa_lines, edges) fail a joint build, the reads the joint choice moved in the failing lines go to work/joint_exclude.txt (priced as a failed gate); `./x <slug> narrate` loops choose -> line ASR -> gates -> exclude, at most 12 rounds, stops when nothing new is excluded. A line with every moved read excluded is narrate.py's pick.
- x: `JOINT=1 SEEDS=2 ./x <slug> narrate`; uv gets praat-parselmouth only when JOINT is set.

DEVIATION FROM THE BEAD TEXT (with the evidence): "consensus of 2 trackers" is Praat for the costs + a Viterbi autocorrelation path as a held-out second tracker (counted beside Praat's in the run's `joint:` line; a terminal event needs both). Reason, measured on chapter 02 (12 joins of narrate.py's picks): On 10 of the 12 joins Praat reads the previous sentence's ending at 62-75 Hz (the others 91 and 114); narrate.py's autocorrelation tracker (folded) reads those sentences' endings at 87-163 Hz and the Viterbi path at 92-255 Hz. Against Praat, mean(Praat - folded autocorr) = +8.8 st, within 3 st on 2 of 12 joins; mean(Praat - Viterbi) = +6.1 st, within 3 st on 1 of 12. Joins past +12 st: Praat 5, folded autocorr 0, Viterbi 2. My first version (min of the two numpy trackers) therefore moved 2 of 21 sentences and saw "0 bad joins before"; the research's gate (T-007, skill G9) is Praat's. --joint needs `uv run --with praat-parselmouth` and says so if it is missing.

REAL DATA (build host; chapter 02 of Video F, P-2's 21 sentences x 5 reads, copies in a scratch dir, P-2's own directory untouched)
- narrate.py's pick vs --joint, Praat on each sentence as assembled (edit() output): joins past +12 st 5 -> 0 of 12; median reset +11.7 -> +8.1 st; max +23.2 -> +11.9; creaky endings 17 -> 11 of 21 (MaroonMarsh's P-2 numbers: 17 -> 11); held-out second tracker: 2 -> 0 of 12; 14 of 21 sentences differ from narrate.py's pick; 19 of 21 picks equal MaroonMarsh's P-2 round-2 picks (narrate.py's own picks equal them on 7 of 21).
- Line-level loop on the real takes: round 0: qa_lines 0.995 PASS, validate PASS, edges FAIL "02_4.0: first word 'but' is not in the line's transcript" (the lost "But" of P-2; the read is the doubled-quote wrap, tag 02_4__s0__a5f6adb7, the same tag MaroonMarsh excluded). `exclude` priced that one read; round 1: qa_lines mean 1.000, validate PASS, edges PASS. One exclusion round, as in P-2's two.
- Real ftts, seeds: "Take thirty-five times five." (michael, 0.1.11) = 1.81 s unseeded, 2.12 s seed 1, 2.35 s seed 2; the quoted wraps likewise (3.51 / 2.48 / 2.05 s; 2.67 / 2.96 / 1.86 s). A fresh `synth` into a second work dir from the same seeds.tsv gave byte-identical files for all 6 seeded reads (md5 equal). Calls went through the lock wrapper.

TESTS (all green on the build host in a clean tree built from the committed content, mode of narration.py aside)
- tools/test_narration_joint.py, 32 tests, run with `uv run --no-project --with numpy --with praat-parselmouth`: Viterbi = brute force over 40 random layered problems; a planted 13.6 st join is avoided (the way out costs 0.02 in score); with every extra cost zero it equals narrate.py's stable-sort pick (50 random score sets with ties); each node cost (gates, hole, rise, question exempt, creak, terminal needs both trackers, extra onset); join cost = Praat's reset, second tracker held out, price starts past +12 st, register step; both trackers on synthetic buzz (glide, strong second harmonic, a 15 st terminal jump, silence); seed tags; `plan --seeds` leaves takes.tsv and the unseeded plan.json byte-identical and a later plan without --seeds restores them; `synth` against a stand-in ftts (right --seed per read, second synth calls nothing); `choose --joint` end to end on a two-sentence line (moves the second sentence off a +15.7 st join to a +9.0 st one, reports `joint.from`, first sentence's samples unchanged; a director's pick kept; where no join is bad the line WAV and report.json are byte-identical to the run without --joint); the exclusion loop converges to narrate.py's pick and never excludes it.
- tools/test_driver.py, +4 tests: the narrate command with every tool a recorder: without JOINT/SEEDS the call sequence is plan, synth, choose, edges and no --seeds/--joint/praat; with both, plan has --seeds=2, choose runs twice with --joint after one exclude; stops when exclude finds nothing new; gives up after 12 rounds.
- Also green on the same tree: test_narration_picks 4, onset 6, edges 5, sibilant 7, test_driver 30 in all. ubs: 0 critical on the four files. No Rust touched: no cargo, clippy or bcheck run, and none claimed.

NOT DONE / OPEN
- Nobody has listened. Whether the joint reads sound better, and whether creak is a defect (the creak weight 1.0 is P-2's), are the owner's A/B.
- Weights are P-2's one-shot, untuned; register 0.1/st, terminal 2.0, hole 1.0 and onset 1.0 are mine and unvalidated against his ear. The extra-onset cue is ASR-based (a heard word before the first scripted one), tested on text, not yet on a real 14_3.0-type take; terminal events fire on synthetic buzz but chapter 02 holds none to move.
- Only chapter 02 measured on real takes (MaroonMarsh has chapter 07 running). Seeds are not yet used on a real video: a SEEDS=N run synthesizes (1+N) x reads and needs the lock.
- `synth` carries a copy of tts_batch.synth's body (it must add --seed); an upstream `--seed` in tts_batch.py would remove the copy (skills repo, not this bead).
- exclude only prices reads the joint choice moved; a failing line whose failing read is narrate.py's own stays red, as it did.
- AGENTS.md doctrine 5 already says seeds are live (1b5ed02); the narration skill's SCORING-AND-SELECTION still says narrate.py choose picks per sentence, until the joint choice is ported there ("portable to the skill's narrate.py": tools/narration.py is a wrapper around it, the DP functions are pure and move as they are).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
SunnyMarsh, independent review of 5933b2f (choose --joint, plan --seeds, synth, exclude, x), 2026-10-14.
VERDICT: the three requested checks PASS; ACCEPT the mechanism as opt-in, but FIX the final-s/z regression (H1) before any video turns JOINT on, and correct the "nothing bad at a join => narrate.py's pick" claim (M1). Nothing here is owner-ear evidence.

1. Tests re-run (laptop, SKILL_SCRIPTS = ~/.claude/skills/natural-sounding-narration-with-frankentts/scripts): test_narration_joint.py 32/32 OK (11.7 s); test_driver.py 30/30 OK (the 4 narrate-dispatch ones included); test_narration_edges 5, onset 6, picks 4, sibilant 7 all OK.

2. `choose` without --joint is byte-identical to the old choose (34bbcfa's tools/narration.py), on real data, build host, scratch ~/jmev_orch/sm_review_4kc2/ (studio untouched):
 - P-2's chapter-02 work dir (21 sentences, 4-8 reads each, studio picks): `diff -r out_old out_new` clean, 12 files (9 WAVs, report.json, review.tsv, spoken.tsv).
 - Video E's whole narration/work from the studio (167 sentences): clean, 65 files (62 WAVs + the three).
 The suite itself does not pin this (its "byte-identical" test compares choose with choose --joint under the NEW code). Mutating analyze() to leave a `joint: null` key in the plain report fails 3 tests, so key presence is pinned; order and values are not. Suggest a golden sha1 of report.json + one WAV from the old code on the test fixture.

3. Planted bad join: genuine. Mutating join_cost to return 0 fails 5 tests (the Viterbi unit test and the 16 st CLI case); mutating the exclusion pricing fails 1.

4. Assembled-line re-gate: exists and works on P-2's real case. I replayed x's loop (choose --joint -> line ASR via P-2's lockf fw wrapper -> qa_lines, validate, edges -> exclude) on P-2's work dir: round 0 `edges` FAIL "02_4.0: first word 'but' is not in the line's transcript"; `exclude` wrote 02_4__s0__a5f6adb7 (= P-2's own exclude_tags.txt); round 1 PASS (qa mean match 1.000, edges 0, validate PASS). BUT mutating exclude() to ignore edge_failures entirely leaves all 32 tests green: the suite exercises only the qa.json path, not the lost-first-word path that was P-2's actual failure (see M2).

Effect, measured by my own trackers (T-001..T-004 audit code: Praat cc, Praat ac, pyin_l) on the assembled lines, not the tool's `joint:` line:
 - ch02, the chapter the weights were set on, 4-6 reads per sentence, 14 of 21 sentences moved: joins past +12 st 4 -> 0 (cc), 4 -> 0 (ac), 4 -> 2 (pyin_l); median +8.5 -> +6.1 / +10.0 -> +7.7 / +9.4 -> +6.8.
 - Video E whole, out of sample, only the 2 existing reads per sentence, 26 of 167 moved: past +12 st 21 -> 18 (cc), 17 -> 14 (ac), 16 -> 15 (pyin_l) of ~101 joins; median +8.4 -> +8.6. The tool's own held-out count says 8 -> 7 of 104. Its "by Praat" count (20 -> 14) is the tracker the costs optimise.

FINDINGS
H1 (high) Final s/z gate regresses: Video E 0 -> 2 chosen reads end without their s/z (01_3.1 "tails.", 06_4.3 "chance."), with creak on or off. node_cost prices cut_short and sibilant_missing alike (gate 5.0), so where every candidate fails a gate it trades a cut-short read for one that drops the s/z, which changes the word. The standing bar is `final s/z: 0`; it is printed, not an exit status, and x's loop only reruns on qa_lines/validate/edges, so a JOINT build ships it. Fix: never move from a read with the s/z to one without (or price sibilant_missing well above cut_short), make `choose --joint` fail when its count exceeds narrate.py's, and add a test (the synthetic fixtures have no sibilant case).
M1 (medium) "when nothing at a join is bad it picks narrate.py's read" (module docstring) is false on real reads. In 19 of the 26 moves on Video E and 6 of the 14 on ch02 the pick is the same with the join cost set to 0: the creak cost (1.0; P-2's baseline has 17 of 21 ch02 endings creaky) and the other node costs re-rank reads where no join is bad. With the creak cost off, ch02 still loses the whole >+12 tail with 8 moves instead of 14 and keeps its median (+8.5 -> +8.5); the creak cost adds the other 6 moves and takes the median down 2.4 st. Out of sample with creak off the tail barely moves (cc 21 -> 19, ac 17 -> 16, pyin_l 16 -> 17) and the median rises +0.8 st, so most of Video E's small gain is the creak preference, not join awareness. The commit says creak is "not decided here" yet it is on by default under --joint. Suggest creak default 0 with an opt-in, or say so in the docstring; the "byte-identical where no join is bad" test uses non-creaky buzz (finals 95-110 Hz) and cannot see it.
M2 (medium) Test gap: mutating exclude() to ignore edge_failures survives all 32 tests (the lost-first-word path above); add a CLI case with a clean qa.json and a line transcript missing the first word.
M3 (minor) Weights were fitted on ch02 and judged on ch02; quote the out-of-sample figures above when a video opts in. Also: score mean 0.8547 -> 0.8448, cut-short reads 26 -> 21, stalls 12 -> 7, hesitation reads 27 -> 28 (Video E).
M4 (minor) work/joint_exclude.txt outlives script edits (x says to move it aside; consider keying it to the script's sha).

Scripts and outputs: build host ~/jmev_orch/sm_review_4kc2/ (rv_d1.sh, rv_d2.sh, rv_loop.sh, rv_nodes.py, rv_cands.py, rv_resets.py, rv_nocreak.py, d1/ d2/); the mutation harness copies are in my laptop scratchpad (repo untouched). fw ran only on 18 line WAVs, through P-2's lockf wrapper.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:

H1 final s/z (and the same trade for the other gates)

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Skill fix for after the finals: the joint exclusion loop (narrate.py `exclude`, `x <slug> narrate` JOINT=1) throws away the wrong reads when a line fails on a sentence that keeps its plain pick. Two cases from the finals chain, 2026-10-14 (GentleDog, finals narration QA).

What the loop does (cmd_exclude): for every line that fails a line-level gate (qa_lines or edges) it excludes EVERY read the joint choice moved anywhere in that line, then chooses again; it ends when a failing line has no new moved read. It never asks which sentence of the line failed.

Case F (mental_math, narration b0b69aa): line 02_8 failed on 02_8.0 ("in hundreds" lost its final s in the chosen read, which the review had labelled an ASR format merge). 02_8.0 kept the plain pick, so nothing there could be excluded; the loop excluded all 7 joint reads of the neighbouring 02_8.1 (the ones that start level with the end of "in hundreds") and left the plain 02_8.1 read, a +23.9 st reset (unchanged from the previous narration). Fixed by two picks.tsv rows (e1b0ad3).

Case E (fair_coin, narration of 7a53679): line 01_1 failed edges on 01_1.2, first word 'alice' not in the line's transcript ("Elise"; the take-level ASR of that read says the same: ratio 0.944, 'Elise and Bob'). SEEDS=2 had added a seed-2 read in the “…” wrap with the best plain score (0.962), so it was the plain pick and not "moved". The loop excluded the four joint reads of 01_1.3 and ran 5 rounds to exit 1 with the line still failing. Fixed by two picks.tsv rows (fbe959c; the second, 06_6.0, a '1-3-3-1' line-ASR format alarm that appeared when the plain pick moved to a seeded read). Proof of the fix is a scratch run of the loop with the rows: 2 rounds, exit 0, 01_1.3 gets its joint read back.

Proposed change (narrate.py, skills repo, then x if it calls anything new):
1. cmd_exclude finds the failing SENTENCE of a failing line, not only the line: edges names it (line.sentence); for a qa_lines failure align the line's transcript to the sentences, or attribute by the sentences' own take-level asr_ratio / first-last-word presence in report.json. Exclude only the joint-moved read of that sentence (the lost "But" of P-2 is this case: the moved read of the sentence that lost its first word, or the one before it when the loss is at the join; keep both, they are the two reads the join involves).
2. If the failing sentence keeps its plain pick (or a director's pick), exclude nothing in the line, print "line L sentence j fails on its plain pick <tag>: a picks.tsv row is needed" and exit 1 at once, instead of running rounds that cannot change the outcome.
3. Move the cause earlier: a take-level first/last-word presence check in choose (the same edge test, run on each read's own transcript), priced like the final s/z flag, so a seeded read whose first word is misheard does not become the plain pick at all. Both cases above would then not have needed the loop.
Tests to land with it: a planted failing sentence on a plain pick with a moved neighbour (the neighbour keeps its joint reads, exit 1, message names the sentence); the P-2 lost-first-word case (that sentence's moved read is excluded, as today); a line where two sentences fail.

Interim: GreenCarp's finals script moves work/joint_exclude.*.txt aside whenever picks change, and the narration QA of each video lists the exclusion file against the failing sentences before a re-narrate.

title: Release tooling: ./x <slug> release-fetch + release-check (tools/release.py): the verified final onto the upload machine, and one gate before every upload
description:
## Why

The goal of the project is eleven videos on YouTube; four are Public, E-K are in finals. Every E-K final is rendered and verified on mac-studio (a finals clone: `~/projects/jeffs_math_explainer_videos_finals`, `..._finals2`, ...), but the upload lane (BronzeRidge, the owner's Codex session) uploads from the laptop checkout, from the paths docs/publish/MANIFEST.md names (`explainer_corpus/<slug>/renders/final/<slug>_master.mp4`, the `.en.srt` beside it, `renders/<slug>_thumbnail.png`, `publish/michael/{title,description,tags}.txt`). Nothing moves a verified final to the laptop or checks that what sits there is the cut the upload text describes. Defects already observed:

- 2026-10-14 14:50: the laptop's `mental_math/renders/final/` is F v1 (master md5 ccc684b2..., e1b0ad3, the cut with orphan captions) while the verified final is v2 (finals2, md5 766f2776..., 0720552) and `publish/michael/description.txt` carries v2's chapter times (e4338e1). Uploading would pair the v1 video and captions with v2's chapter list. The laptop copy has no `*.timeline.tsv`, so nothing there can check the pairing.
- A re-render moves chapter starts (F v2: eight starts by 1-3 s), so an upload text filled against one final is wrong for the next.
- Video A's review (R66, 2026-10-13): MANIFEST rows kept v2 md5s on v3 paths; a stale-copy rewrite of MANIFEST once erased peers' rows.
- Protected phrases missing from upload text (E, I, J on 2026-10-14; now caught by youtube_package check, f6ec9ab, but nothing checks the captions' protected rows on the cut being uploaded).
- Thumbnails: `./x <slug> thumbnail` renders only where it is run; E-K's PNGs were absent from the laptop until placed by hand.

## What

`tools/release.py` (stdlib Python, `python3 -I`), wired as `./x <slug> release-fetch` and `./x <slug> release-check`:

1. `fetch SLUG --from HOST:CLONE` (run on the upload machine): copy from the finals clone's `explainer_corpus/SLUG/renders/final/` the master, the SRT and VTT, every `*.timeline.tsv`, and `renders/SLUG_thumbnail.png` (or the name youtube.md's `- Thumbnail:` line gives) into the local checkout. Before overwriting, an existing `renders/final/` whose master differs is moved aside to `renders/final_vN/` (the next free N; MANIFEST's "preserve before any recut" rule); never deletes. Copies with scp to a temp name in the same directory, checks md5 against the host's (`md5 -q` / `md5sum` over ssh), then renames. Prints the md5 of each file and the git sha of the clone (`git -C CLONE log -1 --format=%h`). A thumbnail missing on the host is reported with the command that renders it (`./x SLUG thumbnail` in the clone, on the build host; nothing compiles on the laptop).
2. `check SLUG` (no network): exit 1 with one line per problem, PASS line otherwise:
   - files: master, SRT, VTT, at least one timeline, the thumbnail youtube.md names.
   - master: ffprobe 3840x2160, 60 fps; duration = sum of timelines' frames/fps within 0.1 s (the cut matches its timelines).
   - upload text: `youtube_package.check(SLUG, finals=renders/final)` (YouTube limits, byte-for-byte block, chapter times = this final's, protected description/title phrases).
   - captions: SRT parses, indices 1..n, times rise, last cue ends within the master's duration; VTT carries the same cue texts; every docs/protected.tsv row whose <where> names `captions` stands in the SRT's cue text (protected_check.py's matching; only 1 such row in the corpus on 2026-10-14, so this is cheap insurance, not the captions check). The SRT-against-script wording check (word for word, spelled numbers, lexicon respellings) is final_check's (mx-tkp6): release-check runs it when tools/final_check.py exists and fails on its DEFECT lines.
   - master vs timelines tolerance 0.1 s: measured on F v2 (finals2), timelines sum 934.817 s, master 934.816 s (format and audio stream).
   - thumbnail: PNG signature, IHDR 1280x720, at most 2 MB (YouTube's limit).
   - MANIFEST: if docs/publish/MANIFEST.md has a row naming this master's path, the md5 written there equals the file's (catches R66's stale md5s); absent row is a note, not a failure (rows are written after upload).
   - prints the md5s and paths to record in MANIFEST, so the row is copied from the tool, not retyped.
   - on PASS prints the upload sheet the upload lane works from: title (title.txt), the description and tags files, the thumbnail and captions paths, category Education, not made for kids, visibility Private (owner's review first), altered/synthetic content Yes with youtube.md's disclosure line, and the master's length, md5 and the clone sha it came from. One checked output instead of reading youtube.md and MANIFEST side by side.

## Tests (tools/test_release.py, unittest, fixture dirs in a temp root, nothing deleted)

Positive: a fixture final (the master check takes an injectable probe function, so the unit tests need no 4K file; one test also probes a 2-frame 3840x2160 MP4 made by `ffmpeg -f lavfi testsrc` when ffmpeg is on PATH, skipped otherwise) plus timelines, SRT/VTT, a 1280x720 PNG, and a package that passes -> PASS.
Planted negatives, each failing alone with its own line: chapter times from another final (one timeline's frames changed by 120); master duration 2 s off its timelines; SRT missing a captions-tagged protected phrase; thumbnail 1280x719; thumbnail over 2 MB; MANIFEST md5 differs; VTT text differs from SRT; SRT cue past the master's end. Fetch: preserve-before-overwrite moves the old final to final_v1 then final_v2 on a second differing fetch (local "host" simulated by a copy function injected for the test); identical fetch moves nothing.
E2E (logged, by hand on the laptop): `./x mental_math release-fetch --from mac-studio:~/projects/jeffs_math_explainer_videos_finals2` then `./x mental_math release-check` -> PASS on F v2; the v1 folder sits at final_v1. Log the commands and outputs in the bead.

## Boundaries

No upload, no visibility change, no MANIFEST edit (the tool prints rows; the upload lane writes them from Studio's state). Read-only on the build host. The full delivery check of the render itself (loudness, chapter lengths, caption-vs-script wording) is final_check's (separate bead); release-check calls it when present.
close_reason: Landed in 8fbf84d (tools/release.py fetch + check with 12 tests) and 69d5e17 (./x release-fetch and release-check integration). Verified E2E against mental_math v2 (0720552) PASS.

Produce Video I, working title "Proofs You Can See", from the owner's request: "let's do another
one about the very best "visual proofs" in math", with his thread of four favourites (Nicomachus's
sum of cubes as slabs tiling a square; 1/4 + 1/16 + ... = 1/3 in a quartered square; (a + b)^2,
^3, ^4 as coloured blocks; Man-Keung Siu's three staircase stacks for the sum of squares). The
owner's four plus the best classics, each animated as a real proof (pieces move into place, then
what was shown and what the picture assumed), quizzes with a countdown, and an honest coda: a
picture can lie (Curry's missing square) and what turns a picture into a proof. This lane runs
P0-P5 (brief, facts + oracle, storyboard + R1, script, build, drafts read as contact and cue
sheets) and stops for the owner; narration, score and 4K follow his review. Voice michael;
12-16 min; chapters <= 85 s. Crate: explainer_corpus/visual_proofs.

comments.author: MaroonMarsh
comments.text:
CITATION CHECK, Video I: Siu and Moser (MaroonMarsh, read only; descriptions are held by GoldenMountain/GrayCave, nothing edited). Asked by GreenCarp for the owner. Both citations are right; two small upgrades below.

1. SIU
CLAIM. description.md l.76-: "Man-Keung Siu, *Mathematics Magazine* 57(2), March 1984, p. 92 [S8]: three stacks of n levels fit a box n by n + 1 by n + 1/2 once the cubes that stick out on top are sliced flat and their upper halves turned into the empty half; so 1^2 + ... + n^2 = 1/3 n (n + 1)(n + 1/2) = n(n + 1)(2n + 1) / 6."
SOURCES (seen). (a) Crossref record, DOI 10.1080/0025570x.1984.11977083: title "Proof without words: Sum of squares", author Siu, Man-Keung, affiliation University of Hong Kong, Mathematics Magazine 57(2), pages 92-92, March 1984. (b) R. B. Nelsen, Proofs Without Words: Exercises in Visual Thinking (MAA, 1993), p. 77, "Sums of Squares I", credit "-Man-Keung Siu"; Nelsen's source list says "77 Mathematics Magazine, vol. 57, no. 2 (March 1984), p. 92." I read the page image (an Internet Archive scan): the caption is 1^2 + 2^2 + ... + n^2 = 1/3 n(n + 1)(n + 1/2); the figure is three stacks (pyramids of cubes with n levels) laid into a box labelled n, n + 1 and n + 1/2, the top layer drawn with half-height pieces and a notch. NOT seen: the 1984 printed page itself.
MATCH. Citation exact (title, volume, issue, month, year, page, Hong Kong). Formula correct: 1/3 n(n+1)(n+1/2) = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6. The figure agrees with "three stacks ... box n by n+1 by n+1/2". The sentence about slicing the top and turning the upper halves into the empty half is the video's reading of a figure that carries no words, and is consistent with the drawing (the top layer's half-height pieces and the notch). Note Nelsen lists J. O. Chilaka's items on other pages (76, 80, 138): the fact sheet's warning about Chilaka's same-title note, 56(2), 1983, p. 90, is right.
FIX. None to the description. docs/fact-sheet.md S8 can drop "no printed figure was looked at": write "Crossref record; Nelsen 1993 p. 77, page image read (three stacks, box n, n+1, n+1/2, caption 1/3 n(n+1)(n+1/2)), source line "Mathematics Magazine, vol. 57, no. 2 (March 1984), p. 92"; the 1984 printed page not seen". "Published this picture in 1984" (08_5) is then supported by Nelsen's attribution, still not by a dated first sight of the printed page.

2. MOSER
CLAIM. description.md l.171-: "The pattern is in Leo Moser's note "On the Danger of Induction", *Mathematics Magazine* 23(2), November-December 1949, p. 109 [S1, F-X.moser]"; "Not said: ... that Moser proved or named the circle problem."
SOURCE (seen). Mathematics Magazine 23(2), November-December 1949, the Internet Archive scan (item sim_mathematics-magazine_november-december-1949_23_2), OCR text. The note sits in the "MATHEMATICAL MISCELLANY" column ("Edited by Charles K. Robbins"), is headed "On the Danger of Induction" and signed "University of North Carolina. Leo Moser"; the next page header is "110 MATHEMATICS MAGAZINE (Nov.-Dec.", so the note is on p. 109.
QUOTE. "Let f(n) be the number of regions determined in the inside of a circle by joining n points on the circumference in all possible ways by straight lines, no three of which are concurrent inside the circle. It is easy to check that f(n) = 1,2,4,8,16, for n = 1,2,3,4,5; and it seems natural to suppose that f(n) = 2^(n-1). However if we go to n = 6 we find that f(6) = 31. We leave it to the reader to show that the correct result for n>1 is actually f(n) = [a sum of binomial coefficients; garbled in the OCR]".
MATCH. Journal, volume, issue, date, page, author, title, the sequence 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, then 31 at six points, and the no-three-concurrent condition: all as in the description. "Moser did not prove or name the circle problem": consistent, he leaves the formula to the reader and gives no name. Secondary sources cite the same item differently: Wikipedia and OEIS A000127 give "Moser, Leo; Ross, W. Bruce, 'Mathematical Miscellany', Mathematics Magazine 23(2), 109-114" (Wikipedia: JSTOR 3219224, not checked by me). That is the column's page range and a co-credit the scan does not show (the scan shows Robbins as column editor and Moser alone signing the note); a JSTOR search will find the column, not the note's title. Crossref has no record for the 1949 item, so the fact sheet's S1 cannot lean on Crossref.
FIX (optional, to help the next reader): "Leo Moser, "On the Danger of Induction", in the "Mathematical Miscellany" column, *Mathematics Magazine* 23(2), November-December 1949, p. 109 (the column runs pp. 109-114)". Nothing in the video's claims changes.

title: Video I (visual_proofs): release: the verified final fetched and release-checked on the upload machine, uploaded Private for the owner's review, Public + MANIFEST + README row on the owner's word
description:
## Why

The finish line for Video I (`visual_proofs`): its verified 4K60 final on YouTube, Public, in the owner's channel, with its upload text, chapters, captions and thumbnail, and recorded. The four released videos had this as their ".16 release" bead (e.g. mx-e-a-8y5.16); E-K's epics stop at finals (mx-e-a-dza.11) and thumbnail + package (mx-e-a-dza.12), so nothing tracked the last step. Owner decisions that bind it (docs/publish/MANIFEST.md, 2026-10-12): voice `michael` for all; every cut is uploaded **Private for the owner's review first**; Public only on the owner's explicit word; only the upload lane (BronzeRidge, the owner's Codex session, from its own Chrome) uploads, edits metadata or changes visibility. Agents prepare and check; they never upload.

## Steps

1. Final verified on the build host (mx-e-a-dza.11 closed or its verify line `visual_proofs verify (<sha>) ... exit 0` in ~/jmev_orch/finals/status.log) and the delivery check posted on mx-e-a-dza.11 (final_check: ffprobe gates, loudness, chapter lengths, captions vs script; blank_stretches; band_dwell).
2. Upload text's chapter times filled from THIS final: `python3 -I tools/youtube_package.py fill visual_proofs --finals <scratch copy of the final's *.timeline.tsv>`, committed (a re-render moves starts: F v2 moved eight by 1-3 s).
3. On the laptop: `./x visual_proofs release-fetch --from mac-studio:<finals clone>` (brings master, SRT, VTT, timelines, thumbnail; preserves an older final as final_vN), then `./x visual_proofs release-check` -> PASS. Post its output (md5s, paths) on this bead.
4. Hand to the upload lane: MANIFEST "Ready, not uploaded" row from release-check's printed md5s (edited from the repo's current copy, never a stale copy), a note to BronzeRidge/GreenCarp with the paths.
5. Upload lane uploads Private: title.txt, description.txt, tags.txt, thumbnail, captions (English, the SRT), category Education, not made for kids, altered/synthetic content Yes (youtube.md's disclosure line). Record the link from Studio's state (Private, SD/HD/4K processed, SRT Published) in MANIFEST's Uploads table.
6. Owner reviews. If the owner asks for a fix: preserve the cut (final -> final_reviewN), fix, re-render, back to step 1 (new chapter times, new md5s). If the owner says Public: the upload lane flips it, MANIFEST row -> **Public** with the date, README's corpus row -> Published with the link and the measured length/LUFS (as rows 1-4).
7. GitHub Release asset for the cut: see the GitHub Releases bead (owner approval, G10).

## Done when

The video is Public at a youtu.be link recorded in MANIFEST with the master's md5, its README corpus row says Published with that link, and release-check PASSed on the exact master that was uploaded (its md5 equals MANIFEST's). Closed by the upload lane or GreenCarp with that evidence, not by the preparing agent.

title: Video E (fair_coin): unify 3D-bulged Flip across 03_3, 05_2, and 08_4, wire chapter moods and Theme::Open/Theme::Resolved in score.rs, and rebuild stems + scored draft
description:
## Background & Motivation
In Video E (`explainer_corpus/fair_coin`), commit `90693cf` guarded the midpoint (`|e - 0.5| < 0.01`) of the custom `Flip` animation in `src/chapters/every_coin.rs:190-220` (`03_3`), which reflects the `HT` region across the `x = y` diagonal with a 3D-like normal bulge `(-1, 1)/sqrt(2) * 0.25 * sin(pi * e)` so the polygon does not collapse to a collinear segment at `e = 0.5`.

However, two later chapters perform the exact same conceptual symmetry reflection across the diagonal using raw `fmn::Transform::new` (linear 2D point interpolation):
1. `src/chapters/where_it_breaks.rs:658` (beat `05_2`, reflecting the `HT` box into the `TH` box across the diagonal to show their areas are unequal when `p != 0.5`).
2. `src/chapters/loaded_dice.rs:623, 646` (beat `08_4`, reflecting the `1-then-2` and `1-then-3` cells across the main diagonal of the 6×6 die table).
Under linear 2D `Transform::new`, every vertex `(x_i, y_i)` moves linearly to `(y_i, x_i)`, so at `e = 0.5` every vertex satisfies `x_i(0.5) = y_i(0.5) = (x_i + y_i)/2`: the entire rectangle collapses onto the 1D line `y = x` (zero area) mid-animation!

Additionally, in `explainer_corpus/fair_coin/src/score.rs:28-29`, `moods: &[]` and `themes: &[]` are currently empty slices, whereas sibling videos (`mental_math`, `bayesian_search`, `eigen_engineering`) populate per-chapter `Mood` transitions and `Theme::Open` / `Theme::Resolved` listen-window cues so `explainer_score` voices the opening motif and closing resolution at the video's structural bookends.

## Implementation Steps
1. **Unify `Flip` in `src/chapters/draw.rs`:**
   - Promote `Flip` from `every_coin.rs:190-220` into `draw.rs` (accepting `from: MobjectId`, `to: MobjectId`, `duration: f64`, and an optional bulge amplitude or default `0.25` along `(-1.0, 1.0) / sqrt(2)` with midpoint guard `if (e - 0.5).abs() < 0.01 { e += 0.01; }`).
   - Replace `Transform::new(ht_ghost, th_target, 1.4)` in `where_it_breaks.rs:658` (`05_2`) and `Transform::new(from_a, to_a, 1.2)` / `Transform::new(from_b, to_b, 1.2)` in `loaded_dice.rs:623, 646` (`08_4`) with `draw::Flip::new(...)`.
2. **Wire `moods` and `themes` in `src/score.rs`:**
   - Populate `themes: &[("01_5", Theme::Open), ("10_4", Theme::Resolved)]` (matching the listen windows in `01_the_gamblers_problem` and `10_how_good_is_it` / `11_your_pocket_has_no_coin`).
   - Populate chapter `moods` across chapters `01..11` matching the narrative progression (e.g. `Mood::Wonder` -> `Mood::Bright` -> `Mood::Tension` on `05_where_it_breaks` -> `Mood::Calm` / `Mood::Bright` on resolution).
3. **Rebuild Stems & Scored Draft on the Build Host:**
   - Because `score::identity()` changes `score::fingerprint(identity, timeline)`, re-render chapters `03`, `05`, `08` at 540p (`./x fair_coin draft 03`, `05`, `08`), then run `./x fair_coin score` (verifying all 11 chapters pass Score QA with narrator F0 `75.5-163.3 Hz` clear) and `./x fair_coin scored`.

## Verification & Testing Requirements
- Unit test in `draw.rs` proving that `Flip` keeps polygon shoelace area strictly bounded away from zero across 100 sampled values `e in [0.0, 1.0]`.
- Unit test in `score.rs` verifying `identity.themes` contains `Theme::Open` and `Theme::Resolved`, `identity.moods` is non-empty, and zero minor-ninth clashes occur against the progression chords.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `./x fair_coin facts-check`, and `ubs` clean.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Move/expose 3D-bulged Flip (with midpoint guard |e - 0.5| < 0.01 and normal bulge) in explainer_corpus/fair_coin/src/chapters/draw.rs and use it in every_coin.rs (03_3), where_it_breaks.rs:658 (05_2), and loaded_dice.rs:623,646 (08_4). 2. Populate moods and themes (01_5 Theme::Open, 10_4 Theme::Resolved) in fair_coin/src/score.rs. 3. Add unit tests for non-zero Flip polygon area across e in [0, 1] and score themes/moods. 4. Re-render affected chapters (03, 05, 08), re-run ./x fair_coin score (11/11 QA pass) and ./x fair_coin scored, and verify contact sheets.
close_reason: Verified by GreenCarp at df6927c (clean git archive on the build host): SunnyMarsh's df6927c makes one Flip for 03_3, 05_2 and 08_4 (05_2's and 08_4's copies no longer fold flat; every drawn frame keeps >= 2% of the area, the edge-on frame is not drawn, the unguarded path has area 0, all tested) and wires E's chapter moods and themes against the real code and storyboard (the bead's struct names, line numbers and theme labels did not match the code; the deviations are recorded in the commit). cargo test -p fair_coin_explainer 39 passed, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, facts-check 277/277 + description 161 numbers 0 unmatched PASS. E's stems and scored draft are rebuilt by chain_e on the build host (after K); SunnyMarsh checks the Flip frames on it.

comments.text:
Refinement Round 1 (Exact Code Anchors & Mathematical Details):
1. every_coin.rs:190-220 defines struct Flip { from: MobjectId, to: MobjectId, duration: f64 } which interpolates corresponding points across the diagonal x = y with normal offset (-1.0, 1.0) / sqrt(2) * 0.25 * (pi * e).sin() and midpoint guard if (e - 0.5).abs() < 0.01 { e += 0.01; }.
2. Move struct Flip into src/chapters/draw.rs (pub struct Flip) and replace:
   - src/chapters/where_it_breaks.rs:658 (beat 05_2): stage.play(Transform::new(ht_ghost, th_target, 1.4)) -> stage.play(draw::Flip::new(ht_ghost, th_target, 1.4))
   - src/chapters/loaded_dice.rs:623, 646 (beat 08_4): Transform::new(from_a, to_a, 1.2) and Transform::new(from_b, to_b, 1.2) -> draw::Flip::new(...)
3. In src/score.rs:28-29, replace moods: &[] and themes: &[] with:
   - themes: &[("01_5", Theme::Open), ("10_4", Theme::Resolved)]
   - moods covering the 11 chapters (e.g. 01 Wonder, 03 Bright, 05 Tension, 06 Calm, 08 Bright, 10 Calm, 11 Bright).
4. Note on stem invalidation: changing score::identity() changes score::fingerprint(identity, timeline), which Kit::finish checks when mixing scored chapters. Therefore ./x fair_coin score MUST be re-run before ./x fair_coin scored.

comments.text:
Refinement Round 3 (Planted-Negative Test Rigor & Swarm Build-Host Verification):
- Every new unit test added for this bead MUST be negative-checked against the pre-fix behaviour (Honest Credit rule in AGENTS.md): verify the test fails when the old behaviour is planted (e.g. linear Transform at e=0.5 in fair_coin; frozen waver in mental_math 04_4; missing Theme::Resolved or minor-ninth clash in lie_robotics; late 13_3 lower-third in matrix_exponential; fade_in point-count resize in explainer_kit / eigen_engineering).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
SunnyMarsh: DONE mx-e-a-e-e-k23.10, df6927c on main (pushed). Five files, pathspec commit: fair_coin draw.rs, every_coin.rs, where_it_breaks.rs, loaded_dice.rs, score.rs.

WHAT CHANGED
- draw.rs: the shared `Flip` (new / between / flipped / flipped_point; LIFT_SHARE, LIFT_BY, EDGE_ON). 03's blocks build theirs through every_coin.rs's `flip_of_block` (same motion as before); 05_2 and 08_4 (the single cell and the whole green triangle, one tracker) call `Flip::between`.
- score.rs: themes ("01_2", Open), ("11_3", Resolved); moods by act (limits 04-05, grows 06-09, settled 10-11; acts I keep the identity's progression). A first draft for the score bead's ear.

THE BEAD'S INACCURACIES (what I followed instead)
1. The Flip it describes does not exist. 90693cf's code is `struct Flip { turn, anchor, parts }` built from a block, with lines and riders, driven by one tracker; its guard skips the frame within 0.01 of edge-on (`(e - 0.5).abs() >= 0.01`), and the lift is LIFT_BY 0.14 before the turn. There is no `Flip{from, to, duration}`, no 0.25 * sin(pi e) bulge and no `e += 0.01`. It is also used in 03_2 (twice) and 03_3, not only 03_3.
2. "Polygon area strictly bounded away from zero over e in [0, 1]" is impossible for any straight-line mirror flip: the area is |1 - 2e| of the shape's, nil at e = 0.5, and a lift or bulge is a translation, which keeps a flat shape flat. The tests state what does hold: every frame the flip draws has area >= 2% of the shape's (exactly |1 - 2e|, 10,001 turns), the edge-on frame is not drawn, and without the guard the unguarded path has area < 1e-9.
3. Call-site lines and names: the raw Transforms were at where_it_breaks.rs:658 (`Transform::new(ghost, mirror).rt(1.7)`) and loaded_dice.rs:623 and 646 (`ghost, mirror` at 1.5 and 1.8 s, the second over 15 cells), not `ht_ghost, th_target` / `from_a, to_a`.
4. score.rs: `moods: &[]` / `themes: &[]` are `Vec::new()` on an `Identity`; `Mood::Wonder / Bright / Tension / Calm` do not exist (a Mood is name, chapters, progression, pedal, swing).
5. Themes at 01_5 and 10_4 would match no window: the kit.listen windows are 01_2, 02_8, 03_2, 05_2, 06_6 and 11_3, and the storyboard's two motif windows are 01_2 ("the motif: two notes, then the same two swapped") and 11_3 ("the motif, resolved"). The test ties the themes to the storyboard's listen column and to the labels in call_it.rs and the_fair_coin_inside.rs.
6. "Sibling videos populate moods": mental_math, bayesian_search and eigen_engineering have `moods: Vec::new()`; only the core crate's own identities (capture_recapture and the others) do.
7. "Zero minor-ninth clashes against the progression chords" has no defined subject here (fair_coin has no sonification files). The test uses `explainer_score::score::clashes` on what the themes sound: the open motif over chapter 01's chords, the resolution over chapter 11's. The identity's own Gmaj9 puts its F# a semitone under the resolution's 1, which is why chapter 11 has the settled mood.

EVIDENCE (build host, clean tree of HEAD plus the five files, ~/jmev_scratch/fair_coin_sm_1)
- ./x fair_coin test: fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, 39 tests: exit 0. facts-check 277 against 277 oracle keys PASS. ubs 0 critical. scan_private clean.
- Planted negatives, each failing the named tests: guard removed -> 3 draw.rs tests (pure and stage); 05_2 or 08_4 back to Transform -> the wiring test; themes at 01_5/10_4 or none -> the themes test; chapter 11 off its mood -> the clash test and the mood test. One slip: my "no moods" plant did not compile (my syntax); moods-empty is covered by the assert and by the chapter-11 plant, not by a mutant run.
- 540p drafts of 03, 05 and 08, layout lint 0 findings; the flips read on 10 fps montages of the drafts (lift, an edge-on sliver beside the diagonal, landing): 05_2 (18.0-19.5 s), 08_4 (the cell, then the sheet), 03_2 and its listen-window flip. Montages: laptop scratchpad m05_flip.png, m05_2.png, m08_4.png, m03.png; draft sheets under the scratch tree's renders/draft/.
- ./x fair_coin score: Score QA PASS 11/11, narrator F0 75.5-163.3 Hz (music keeps out of 67.2-194.2 Hz). The stems differ from the studio's where meant: chapter 01 only in seconds 16-19 (the 01_2 window), 04 and 11 throughout, 02 not at all. ./x fair_coin scored: all 11 chapters at 960x540@60; watch file 726.0 s, md5 ce0a3155 (scratch only).
- Not done: the studio checkout's stems and renders still carry the old empty moods/themes; after a pull there run `./x fair_coin score && ./x fair_coin scored && ./x fair_coin watch scored`. No scored-draft joins check run; no owner listening.
- Process note: I renamed Flip::build's three call sites first with a sed and, on GreenCarp's order, redid them with the Edit tool before committing (revert, then forward).

title: Video E (fair_coin): release: the verified final fetched and release-checked on the upload machine, uploaded Private for the owner's review, Public + MANIFEST + README row on the owner's word
description:
## Why

The finish line for Video E (`fair_coin`): its verified 4K60 final on YouTube, Public, in the owner's channel, with its upload text, chapters, captions and thumbnail, and recorded. The four released videos had this as their ".16 release" bead (e.g. mx-e-a-8y5.16); E-K's epics stop at finals (mx-e-a-e-e-k23.11) and thumbnail + package (mx-e-a-e-e-k23.12), so nothing tracked the last step. Owner decisions that bind it (docs/publish/MANIFEST.md, 2026-10-12): voice `michael` for all; every cut is uploaded **Private for the owner's review first**; Public only on the owner's explicit word; only the upload lane (BronzeRidge, the owner's Codex session, from its own Chrome) uploads, edits metadata or changes visibility. Agents prepare and check; they never upload.

## Steps

1. Final verified on the build host (mx-e-a-e-e-k23.11 closed or its verify line `fair_coin verify (<sha>) ... exit 0` in ~/jmev_orch/finals/status.log) and the delivery check posted on mx-e-a-e-e-k23.11 (final_check: ffprobe gates, loudness, chapter lengths, captions vs script; blank_stretches; band_dwell).
2. Upload text's chapter times filled from THIS final: `python3 -I tools/youtube_package.py fill fair_coin --finals <scratch copy of the final's *.timeline.tsv>`, committed (a re-render moves starts: F v2 moved eight by 1-3 s).
3. On the laptop: `./x fair_coin release-fetch --from mac-studio:<finals clone>` (brings master, SRT, VTT, timelines, thumbnail; preserves an older final as final_vN), then `./x fair_coin release-check` -> PASS. Post its output (md5s, paths) on this bead.
4. Hand to the upload lane: MANIFEST "Ready, not uploaded" row from release-check's printed md5s (edited from the repo's current copy, never a stale copy), a note to BronzeRidge/GreenCarp with the paths.
5. Upload lane uploads Private: title.txt, description.txt, tags.txt, thumbnail, captions (English, the SRT), category Education, not made for kids, altered/synthetic content Yes (youtube.md's disclosure line). Record the link from Studio's state (Private, SD/HD/4K processed, SRT Published) in MANIFEST's Uploads table.
6. Owner reviews. If the owner asks for a fix: preserve the cut (final -> final_reviewN), fix, re-render, back to step 1 (new chapter times, new md5s). If the owner says Public: the upload lane flips it, MANIFEST row -> **Public** with the date, README's corpus row -> Published with the link and the measured length/LUFS (as rows 1-4).
7. GitHub Release asset for the cut: see the GitHub Releases bead (owner approval, G10).

## Done when

The video is Public at a youtu.be link recorded in MANIFEST with the master's md5, its README corpus row says Published with that link, and release-check PASSed on the exact master that was uploaded (its md5 equals MANIFEST's). Closed by the upload lane or GreenCarp with that evidence, not by the preparing agent.

description:
## Background & Motivation
Once Video K (`eigen_engineering`) completes `mx-e-a-e-k-oq4.7`, `mx-e-a-e-k-oq4.8`, and `mx-e-a-e-k-oq4.10` (chapters `08–15` P5 dense-read fixes & tests, production re-narration on `HEAD`, score stem build & QA on all 15 chapters, scored 540p watch draft verification, and owner review), this bead executes the Gate G8 4K60 final render, PCM master assembly, and strict verification.

## Production Pipeline & Technical Steps (on the Build Host)
1. **Pre-Flight Gate Check:**
   - Confirm clean git tree (`G8` rejects `--fmn-local` or uncommitted edits).
   - Run `./x eigen_engineering facts-check` (315/315 pass), `cargo test` (190+ tests pass), and `./x eigen_engineering probe` (read the glyph probe sheet).
2. **4K60 Chapter Renders (`./x eigen_engineering final`):**
   - Render all 15 chapters (`01_the_bad_speed` through `15_one_idea`) at `3840x2160 @ 60 fps`, BT.709, single encoder across all chapters.
   - Confirm `layout.tsv` is 0 bytes in all 15 chapters and `cue_check` passes with 0 errors and all chapters `<= 85 s`.
3. **PCM Master Assembly & Captions (`./x eigen_engineering master` & `./x eigen_engineering captions`):**
   - Assemble `explainer_corpus/eigen_engineering/renders/final/eigen_engineering_master.mp4` with PCM master audio and rebuild SRT/WebVTT captions.
4. **Strict G8 Verification (`./x eigen_engineering verify`):**
   - Run `verify_video.sh` (`3840x2160`, `60 fps`, `BT.709`, `-16 LUFS ± 1.0`, `<= -1.0 dBTP`, `A/V <= 0.2 s`, null test, full hardware + software decode).
   - Read all 15 final 4K contact sheets and cue sheets, run `./x eigen_engineering joins final` across all 14 chapter joins, and record MD5 + telemetry in bead comments.
acceptance_criteria: 1. All 15 chapters rendered at 3840x2160 @ 60 fps via ./x eigen_engineering final with a clean git tree (no --fmn-local). 2. PCM master assembled via ./x eigen_engineering master and captions rebuilt via ./x eigen_engineering captions. 3. ./x eigen_engineering verify (verify_video.sh with EXPECT_* gates: 3840x2160, 60 fps, BT.709, -16 LUFS +-1, <= -1.0 dBTP, A/V <= 0.2 s, null test, hardware + software decode) passes 100%. 4. All 15 final 4K contact sheets and cue sheets read and verified.

comments.text:
Refinement Round 1 (Gate G8 4K60 Master & Stem-Reuse Invariants):
1. Encoder & Color-Space Uniformity: Every chapter must be rendered via './x <slug> final' using the shared explainer_kit encoder wrapper (P010 -> BT.709 8-bit stream, 3840x2160 @ 60 fps) with a clean git tree (never --fmn-local; G8 rejects dirty trees or local engine overrides).

4. Strict Verification Gates ('./x <slug> verify'):
   - Resolution: 3840x2160, Frame rate: 60 fps, Color primaries/transfer/matrix: BT.709
   - Integrated loudness: -16.0 LUFS +- 1.0 LU, True peak: <= -1.0 dBTP

title: Video K (eigen_engineering): release: the verified final fetched and release-checked on the upload machine, uploaded Private for the owner's review, Public + MANIFEST + README row on the owner's word
description:
## Why

The finish line for Video K (`eigen_engineering`): its verified 4K60 final on YouTube, Public, in the owner's channel, with its upload text, chapters, captions and thumbnail, and recorded. The four released videos had this as their ".16 release" bead (e.g. mx-e-a-8y5.16); E-K's epics stop at finals (mx-e-a-e-k-oq4.11) and thumbnail + package (mx-e-a-e-k-oq4.12), so nothing tracked the last step. Owner decisions that bind it (docs/publish/MANIFEST.md, 2026-10-12): voice `michael` for all; every cut is uploaded **Private for the owner's review first**; Public only on the owner's explicit word; only the upload lane (BronzeRidge, the owner's Codex session, from its own Chrome) uploads, edits metadata or changes visibility. Agents prepare and check; they never upload.

## Steps

1. Final verified on the build host (mx-e-a-e-k-oq4.11 closed or its verify line `eigen_engineering verify (<sha>) ... exit 0` in ~/jmev_orch/finals/status.log) and the delivery check posted on mx-e-a-e-k-oq4.11 (final_check: ffprobe gates, loudness, chapter lengths, captions vs script; blank_stretches; band_dwell).
2. Upload text's chapter times filled from THIS final: `python3 -I tools/youtube_package.py fill eigen_engineering --finals <scratch copy of the final's *.timeline.tsv>`, committed (a re-render moves starts: F v2 moved eight by 1-3 s).
3. On the laptop: `./x eigen_engineering release-fetch --from mac-studio:<finals clone>` (brings master, SRT, VTT, timelines, thumbnail; preserves an older final as final_vN), then `./x eigen_engineering release-check` -> PASS. Post its output (md5s, paths) on this bead.
4. Hand to the upload lane: MANIFEST "Ready, not uploaded" row from release-check's printed md5s (edited from the repo's current copy, never a stale copy), a note to BronzeRidge/GreenCarp with the paths.
5. Upload lane uploads Private: title.txt, description.txt, tags.txt, thumbnail, captions (English, the SRT), category Education, not made for kids, altered/synthetic content Yes (youtube.md's disclosure line). Record the link from Studio's state (Private, SD/HD/4K processed, SRT Published) in MANIFEST's Uploads table.
6. Owner reviews. If the owner asks for a fix: preserve the cut (final -> final_reviewN), fix, re-render, back to step 1 (new chapter times, new md5s). If the owner says Public: the upload lane flips it, MANIFEST row -> **Public** with the date, README's corpus row -> Published with the link and the measured length/LUFS (as rows 1-4).
7. GitHub Release asset for the cut: see the GitHub Releases bead (owner approval, G10).

## Done when

The video is Public at a youtu.be link recorded in MANIFEST with the master's md5, its README corpus row says Published with that link, and release-check PASSed on the exact master that was uploaded (its md5 equals MANIFEST's). Closed by the upload lane or GreenCarp with that evidence, not by the preparing agent.

comments.text: CORRECTION to my earlier comment and to commits 31bbfe3/01014b9: 'set_points refuses a run of another size' is wrong (SunnyMarsh's probe was right). Probed on a bare stage with set_points's Result printed: it is Ok for 2->49 vertices, points do change. title: Video F (mental_math): drive 04_4 waver continuously through END_HOLD_S, wire 14_3 three-turn three-pluck recall beat, and verify scored draft
description:
## Background & Motivation
In Video F (`explainer_corpus/mental_math`), commit `05a1ba5` fixed the `u64` addition overflow in `model::near_fifty` (`model.rs:302-316`), deduplicated `waver` into `src/chapters/draw.rs`, and added `score.rs` unit tests. Two high-leverage visual/audio polish items remain from the code and storyboard audit:

1. **Frozen `waver` during `04_4`'s `END_HOLD_S` (`src/chapters/by_parts.rs:344`):**
   - In chapter `04_by_parts` (`04_4`), the juggling items' vertical oscillation is driven by an `add_dt_updater` reading a `ValueTracker` (`waver`) that is only advanced when `waver.animate_value(...)` is explicitly played.
   - At line 344, the chapter ends with `kit.music_breath(stage, END_HOLD_S)` (`1.5 s`), which calls `stage.wait_frames(...)` without advancing `waver`. As a result, the juggling balls freeze motionless in mid-air for the final 1.5 seconds of the chapter.
   - Driving `waver` across `END_HOLD_S` (or stepping `waver.animate_value(END_HOLD_S, ...)` inside the breath window while recording the music breath mark) keeps the motion alive right up to the chapter cut.
2. **Closing recall beat `14_3` three-pluck sonification (`src/chapters/near_something_you_know.rs:482`):**
   - In chapter `14` (`14_3`, `near_something_you_know.rs:482`), the closing callback highlights the three core mental-math patterns in sequence (`turns` loop). Wiring this beat with its three-pluck sonification from `src/chapters/sound.rs` (and verifying the `score` timeline marks) gives the visual callback its intended musical punctuation.

## Implementation Steps
1. Update `explainer_corpus/mental_math/src/chapters/by_parts.rs` around line 344 so `waver` advances continuously through `END_HOLD_S` while preserving the chapter's exact frame count and music breath mark.
2. Update `explainer_corpus/mental_math/src/chapters/near_something_you_know.rs` around line 482 (`14_3`) and `src/chapters/sound.rs` so the three-turn visual highlight triggers the three-pluck sonification cleanly.
3. Add unit tests in `by_parts.rs` (verifying non-zero y-displacement of the juggling items across `END_HOLD_S`) and `sound.rs` / `near_something_you_know.rs`.
4. Re-render chapters `04` and `14` on the build host, run `./x mental_math score` (verifying 14/14 chapters pass Score QA) and `./x mental_math scored`, and inspect the updated frames.

In explainer_corpus/mental_math/src/chapters/by_parts.rs:344 (04_4), drive the waver tracker continuously through END_HOLD_S (1.5 s) instead of freezing during music_breath. 2. In near_something_you_know.rs:482 (14_3), pair the three turns of the closing recall beat with the three-pluck sonification from sound.rs. 3. Add unit tests verifying continuous waver motion during 04_4's hold and sound mark/sonification alignment in 14_3. 4. Re-render chapters 04 and 14, re-run ./x mental_math score and ./x mental_math scored, and verify contact sheets.

title: Video F (mental_math): 4K60 finals + PCM master + strict verify_video.sh (G8)
description:
## Background & Motivation
Once Video F (`mental_math`) completes its narration & initial score (`mx-e-a-f-ms4.8`), `04_4` continuous `waver` + `14_3` three-pluck polish (`mx-e-a-f-ms4.10`), and owner review of `renders/mental_math_scored_watch.mp4`, this bead executes the Gate G8 4K60 final render, PCM master assembly, and strict verification.

## Production Pipeline & Technical Steps (on the Build Host)
1. **Pre-Flight Gate Check:**
   - Confirm clean git tree (`G8` rejects `--fmn-local` or uncommitted modifications).
   - Run `./x mental_math facts-check` (300/300 pass), `cargo test`, and `./x mental_math probe` (read the glyph probe sheet).
2. **4K60 Chapter Renders (`./x mental_math final`):**
   - Render all 14 chapters at `3840x2160 @ 60 fps`, BT.709, single encoder across retained and camera routes.
   - Confirm `layout.tsv` is 0 bytes in all 14 chapters and `cue_check` passes with 0 errors and all chapters `<= 85 s`.
3. **PCM Master Assembly & Captions (`./x mental_math master` & `./x mental_math captions`):**
   - Assemble the 4K60 master (`explainer_corpus/mental_math/renders/final/mental_math_master.mp4`) with PCM master audio and rebuild SRT/WebVTT captions.
4. **Strict G8 Verification (`./x mental_math verify`):**
   - Run `verify_video.sh` (`3840x2160`, `60 fps`, `BT.709`, `-16 LUFS ± 1.0`, `<= -1.0 dBTP`, `A/V <= 0.2 s`, null test, full decode).
   - Read all 14 final 4K contact sheets and cue sheets, run `./x mental_math joins final` across all 13 chapter joins, and record MD5 + telemetry in bead comments.
acceptance_criteria: 1. All 14 chapters rendered at 3840x2160 @ 60 fps via ./x mental_math final with a clean git tree (no --fmn-local). 2. PCM master assembled via ./x mental_math master and captions rebuilt via ./x mental_math captions. 3. ./x mental_math verify (verify_video.sh with EXPECT_* gates: 3840x2160, 60 fps, BT.709, -16 LUFS +-1, <= -1.0 dBTP, A/V <= 0.2 s, null test, hardware + software decode) passes 100%. 4. All 14 final 4K contact sheets and cue sheets read and verified.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Refinement Round 1 (Gate G8 4K60 Master & Stem-Reuse Invariants):
1. Encoder & Color-Space Uniformity: Every chapter must be rendered via './x <slug> final' using the shared explainer_kit encoder wrapper (P010 -> BT.709 8-bit stream, 3840x2160 @ 60 fps) with a clean git tree (never --fmn-local; G8 rejects dirty trees or local engine overrides).
2. Stem Frame-Count Lock: Kit::finish verifies that each chapter's rendered frame count matches the scored timeline's exact sample count and score::fingerprint(identity, timeline). If a purely visual positioning tweak is made after scoring without changing any wait/animation duration, verify the chapter frame count is identical so stems remain valid without re-scoring (matching the mx-e-a-8y5.15 pattern).
3. PCM Master & Null Test: './x <slug> master' replays audio cues through the PCM master pipeline (W2-master), verifies the null test against per-chapter stems, and muxes Annex-B video into renders/final/<slug>_master.mp4; './x <slug> captions' generates SRT/WebVTT captions from cue logs.
4. Strict Verification Gates ('./x <slug> verify'):
   - Resolution: 3840x2160, Frame rate: 60 fps, Color primaries/transfer/matrix: BT.709
   - Integrated loudness: -16.0 LUFS +- 1.0 LU, True peak: <= -1.0 dBTP
   - A/V stream duration delta: <= 0.200 s
   - Full software + hardware decode: 0 errors
   - Word-aligned FrankenWhisper join audit ('./x <slug> joins final') across all chapter boundaries + all 4K contact/cue sheets read.

Agents prepare and check; they never upload.

## Steps

1. 4. Hand to the upload lane: MANIFEST "Ready, not uploaded" row from release-check's printed md5s (edited from the repo's current copy, never a stale copy), a note to BronzeRidge/GreenCarp with the paths.

6. Owner reviews. If the owner asks for a fix: preserve the cut (final -> final_reviewN), fix, re-render, back to step 1 (new chapter times, new md5s). If the owner says Public: the upload lane flips it, MANIFEST row -> **Public** with the date, README's corpus row -> Published with the link and the measured length/LUFS (as rows 1-4).
7. GitHub Release asset for the cut: see the GitHub Releases bead (owner approval, G10).

comments.text:
F v2 10:54.6 'And that's Bethe's twenty-three hundred' (BronzeRidge's fw hears 'and that beta is 2300'): targeted check of the actual take; verdict ASR spelling, not a misarticulation (EmeraldOwl, read only, the cut untouched; no ears used: spectrogram, formants, decoys, as the owner's rule says).
- Which take: line 10_2 sentence 2, read 10_2__s2__e2c9356a (clone 1 narration/work/takes; the director's pick in picks.tsv). ftts input 'And that's Bayta's, twenty-three hundred.' (the lexicon's respelling 'Bayta' for Bethe, michael, probed 2026-10-13; the comma keeps the name apart from the number). Its own ASR in the run: 'And that's Betas 2300.'; the assembled line 10_2: '... And that's betas, 2300.' ftts is deterministic: re-running the same input today gives a WAV with the same MD5 as the take (bb452aa98e3cea440a93d988e7dba04f).
- What the take says (Praat, Burg formants on the take): 'And that's' then the stressed syllable with a diphthong: onset F1 643 Hz, F2 1343 Hz, gliding to F1 388, F2 2136 (mid-vowel F1 620, F2 1708), then a schwa at F2 about 1590, then the pause of the comma. That is /eɪ/ then /ə/: BAY-tuh(z), the lexicon's 'say'. The lexicon's own probe numbers for the candidate 'Bayta' were F1 578 to 492, F2 1575 to 1871 and for the decoy 'Beeta' F1 418 to 308, F2 1750 to 2105.
- Decoys through the same voice and pipeline: 'And that's Beeta's, twenty-three hundred.' (BEE-tuh): vowel F1 460 to 300, F2 1581 to 2222 (mid F1 401, F2 2005), i.e. a high front /i/; 'And that's Beth-uh's, ...' (BETH-uh): short steady vowel, F2 1600-1700 with no glide. The take's vowel is 200+ Hz higher in F1 at mid-vowel than Beeta's and has the long F2 glide Beth-uh lacks. Spectrograms of the three read side by side agree (the take's vowel is a diagonal glide).
- ASR on the same three files (fw 0.11.0 on the host, no prompt): the take 'And that's Betas 2300.'; the Beeta decoy 'and that's betas 2300'; the Beth-uh decoy 'And that's Beth Ozz 2300.'. So fw writes the correct BAY-tuh and the wrong BEE-tuh identically as 'betas': it cannot discriminate them, as the lexicon recorded ('Beeta decoy written Beta in 4 of 4, the same as the candidates'; probe.discriminates false; accept list has beta, betas via phrases). 'Bethe' and 'beta' are homophones in this pronunciation (/beɪtə/), so 'beta is' is the spelling any ASR gives it; BronzeRidge's 'that beta is 2300' is that, with the possessive split off.
- Verdict: not an audible misarticulation: the name is BAY-tuhz on the take. A listener hears 'Bethe's' as the video's other mentions (09_1-09_4, 11_4 use the same respelling). If the owner wants the 'beta' look-alike gone from machine transcripts, only the caption or a respelling that changes the sound could do it; the cut is not to be altered on this account.
- Not claimed: how it sounds to the owner; a human listen is still the owner's. (My checks are acoustic and by decoy.)

title: Epic Video H: How to Find a Lost Submarine (bayesian_search)
description:
Produce Video H, working title "How to Find a Lost Submarine", from the owner's request: "Using
Bayesian Statistics to find lost submarines, boaters, etc." with the subject line "A nuclear sub has
gone missing, men are trapped, & time is running out. How can we possibly find them in time?"
The method is the hero: a prior map of cells built from weighted scenarios, detection probability
(the chance of finding = the chance it is there times the chance you would see it), Bayes' rule after
a failed search, planning by where the next effort buys the most (Koopman's random search formula),
and drift under time pressure. Stories, each checked against primary sources: Palomares 1966,
Scorpion 1968 (all 99 men were lost; never implied otherwise), Air France 447 (2011), Coast Guard
rescues. Quizzes with a visible countdown. This lane runs P0-P5 (brief, facts + oracle, storyboard +
R1, script, build, drafts read as contact and cue sheets) and stops for the owner; narration, score
and 4K follow his review. Voice michael; 11-15 min; chapters <= 85 s. Crate:
explainer_corpus/bayesian_search.

description:
## Background & Motivation
In Video H (`explainer_corpus/bayesian_search`), several critical code fixes landed after the initial narrated/scored drafts:
1. **Sound Mark Fixes (`92813d0`, `GrayCave`):**
   - `08_4` (`where_next.rs`): `Lattice::search_silent` for searches 2–4 so `whoosh:search` fires only on the first search (matching the storyboard sound plan).
   - `11_6` (`twelve_hours.rs`): `pizz:found` moved to after `line.wait_end`, in the post-line gap, instead of mid-sentence at `"a helicopter"` (where the score engine skipped it because there was no clear second before the voice).
   - `14_6` (`four_maps.rs`): redundant `resolve:method` mark at sentence onset dropped (the final gap resolves into `14_7`'s window).
   - As `GrayCave` noted on `mx-e-a-h-6ix2.8`: *"the three mark changes are in the chapters, so chapters 08, 11, 14 must be re-rendered (their timelines) before `./x bayesian_search score` for the pluck and the single whoosh to be in the stems; the old timelines still score, with `pizz:found` and `resolve:method` unanswered."*
2. **Dense-Read Visual Fixes (`6b0876f` & `f482b6f`, `GoldenMountain`):**
   - `03_5`: countdown ring no longer crosses `"weight 40"` (cards levelled with the sea's rows, tops under the ring).
   - `06_4`: chip `"the wreck is here and the search missed it"` moved under the ruler, clear of D's `"2 in 3"` / `"6 2/3 %"`.
   - `10_1/10_2`: `"last known position"` moved left of the diamond (three short lines) so it is never covered by the expanding drift cloud's dots and edge circle from `0.5 h` to `7 h`.
   - `12_3`: `"4 empty searches: 1 on the surface, 3 under water"` dwell increased from `1.4 s` to `3.4 s`.
   - `13_1`: paper's letters (`L`, `E`, `SEP`) named once with their meanings and citation, dwell increased from `1.3 s` to `5.0 s` with frame.
   - `13_6`: sonar-zero note wrapped to 3 lines of 38 chars so `"0 is 0"` stays clear of the `94` caption.
