comments.author: MaroonMarsh
comments.text:
CITATION CHECK, Video H (MaroonMarsh, read only; descriptions are held by GoldenMountain/GrayCave, nothing edited). Asked by GreenCarp for the owner. Two parts: Chew's theorem, and the 0.3 question (decisions.md R2 row, description.md ~l.184-196).

PART 1: CHEW, "THEOREM 2.1"
CLAIM. description.md l.81-88: with a fixed object, independent tries of known fixed d_i and equal cost, the rule "is optimal in the strongest sense: for every n, the chance of still not having found it after n searches is as small as any plan can make it (Chew 1967, "A Sequential Search Procedure", Theorem 2.1; the equal-cost case goes back to Blackwell and to Black 1965)". Sources list: "Annals of Mathematical Statistics 38(2), 1967" (no pages), "Information and Control 8, 1965".
SOURCE. M. C. Chew, Jr., "A Sequential Search Procedure", Ann. Math. Statist. 38(2), April 1967, pp. 494-502, DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177698965. SEEN: the Project Euclid record with the full abstract (an archived copy). NOT SEEN: the paper's text. Project Euclid and JSTOR refuse automated fetches (Incapsula), Semantic Scholar lists the PDF as open access but the download is blocked too, and no mirror turned up. So I could not read Theorem 2.1 or confirm its number.
QUOTES (abstract). "An object to be found is located in one of R locations."; "an overlook probability alpha_i ... (0 < alpha_i < 1)"; "it is assumed that all outcomes are independent, conditional on the location of the object and the inspection procedure used"; "It is assumed here that c_i = 1"; "In the next section delta* is shown to be strongly optimal in the sense that P[N > n | delta*] <= P[N > n | delta], for each n = 0, 1, 2, ..., and every search procedure delta"; and "Blackwell (see [3]) has shown that if, in addition, an inspection of i costs c_i, the procedure minimizing the expected searching cost is a one-stage procedure".
Black 1965 (read in full, Information and Control 8(2), pp. 159-162): "a single target is in one of several regions and cannot move"; "Always look in the region for which the posterior probability (given the failure of earlier looks) of finding the object divided by the cost is maximum."
MATCH. The result (every n), its conditions (one object that does not move, independent looks, known fixed overlook probability, unit cost) and the rule (greatest p_i times (1 - alpha_i) after each update) match the abstract. Proved in "the next section", so a Theorem 2.1 is plausible; the number is UNVERIFIED by me. One sentence is off: Blackwell (as Chew reports him) and Black 1965 give the least-EXPECTED-COST rule, with unequal costs; the every-n statement for equal costs is Chew's. "The equal-cost case goes back to Blackwell and to Black" reads as if the every-n result does.
FIX. (a) Sources: "M. C. Chew, Jr., "A Sequential Search Procedure", *Annals of Mathematical Statistics* 38(2), 1967, pp. 494-502" and "W. L. Black, "Discrete Sequential Search", *Information and Control* 8(2), 1965, pp. 159-162". (b) Replace "(Chew 1967, "A Sequential Search Procedure", Theorem 2.1; the equal-cost case goes back to Blackwell and to Black 1965)" with "(Chew 1967, "A Sequential Search Procedure", Theorem 2.1; Blackwell and Black 1965 had the weaker result, the least expected cost, for unequal costs too, by the rule p_i d_i / c_i)". (c) Whoever holds the page images of Chew pp. 494-496 (fact-sheet S11) should confirm "Theorem 2.1" on the page; if the number differs, change it.

PART 2: IS THE DRIFT ERROR 0.3 A PROBABLE ERROR OR A RADIUS THAT HOLDS EVERY POINT?
ANSWER. A PROBABLE ERROR (the radius of the circle that holds half of the possible positions), which the Coast Guard combines with its other errors and then enlarges by a safety factor. It is not a radius that holds every dot.
SOURCES (seen, text read). (1) J. R. Frost and L. D. Stone, Review of Search Theory: Advances and Applications to Search and Rescue Decision Support, USCG R&DC report CG-D-15-01, September 2001 (an archived copy of DTIC ADA397065, 127 pp.). (2) United States National Search and Rescue Supplement to the IAMSAR Manual, National SAR Committee, May 2000, glossary (copy hosted by Civil Air Patrol). NOT SEEN: the IAMSAR Manual Vol. II itself (not freely online); the 2018 NSS PDF refuses fetches (a search snippet of its glossary has the same 0.3 wording).
QUOTES. Frost and Stone p. 4-2: "the probable error is the elliptical (or circular) contour centered on the mean that contains 50 percent of the distribution", e = 1.18 sigma. p. 4-5, step 10: "Estimate the probable error of the mean drift displacement vector as one-eighth of its magnitude. (De = 1/8 of the distance between incident and datum positions.)"; step 12: total probable error E from the root sum of squares; step 13: "Use E with appropriate "safety factors" ... to determine search area size." pp. 4-24 to 4-25 (4.6.1.3 Drift Error Estimation): "Recall that the CSPM began by estimating the probable drift error as one-eighth of the distance drifted."; "This factor was later increased to three-tenths (3/10, 0.3), but even this may have been optimistic."; "...would have to be within 15 percent of its mean value half the time to produce a resultant probable error of 0.3." Table 4-2 (p. 4-16), CSPM search radii: 1.1E, 1.6E, 2.0E, 2.3E, 2.5E for searches 1 to 5, "called "safety factors"" (p. 4-17); p. 4-18: the first search radius 1.1E, "the POC of a square with this inscribed radius is 0.64762", chosen for a first-search POS of about 50 percent.
NSS 2000 glossary: "confidence factor (CF): Value, normally 0.3, applied to account for errors in assumed initial distress position, sea current, wind current, and leeway. Used to determine drift error (de)."; "individual drift error (de): Individual Drift multiplied by Confidence Factor."; "total drift error (De): Also "total probable drift error" or "drift error". The total probable error in the datum position that is contributed by the total drift velocity error"; "total probable error (E): ... the square root of the sum of the squares of the total drift error, initial position error, and search facility error."; "probable error (from statistics): The range on either side of the average or expected value such that the probability of being within that range is 50%."; "optimal search radius ... R = E x fs"; "safety factor (fs): A factor used to enlarge the search area to increase the chance of the search object being in the search area."
MATCH. The description's "(the figure the Coast Guard's review of search theory, Frost and Stone 2001, gives for drift error)" is true but incomplete: Frost and Stone report it as the CSPM's later confidence factor and call it "perhaps optimistic"; it is a probable error. The open paragraph ("not yet checked against the source") can now be closed: the Coast Guard's reading is the second one in it.
WHAT IT DOES TO THE NUMBERS (my arithmetic with the video's own constants: 180 miles of track x 0.1 mile strip = 18 sq mi, random search 1 - e^-coverage, de = 0.3 x 1.5 mi/h x hours, start error 1 mile taken as a probable error and combined as the Coast Guard does, root sum of squares; the video adds them, 1 + 0.45 h). At 1, 3, 6, 12 hours the video's disc gives 93, 65, 34, 13 in 100 (as in the description). The Coast Guard's own first search (a square of half-side 1.1 E, E = 1.10, 1.68, 2.88, 5.49 mi, holding about 65 in 100 of the spread) gives 95, 73, 36, 12. A circle that holds 95 in 100 of a circular normal spread (2.08 E in radius) gives 67, 37, 15, 4; one that holds 99 in 100 (2.58 E) gives 51, 26, 10, 3. So the video's numbers are close to what the Coast Guard's first search square would give, "hours matter" stands, and "in this model" is right; but the dots are not the Coast Guard's distribution (a hard-edged uniform disc, not a circular normal spread whose 50% circle is 0.3 of the distance).
EXACT FIX. In the drift-cloud bullet replace "(the figure the Coast Guard's review of search theory, Frost and Stone 2001, gives for drift error)" with "(the Coast Guard's own planning figure for drift error, a probable error: the radius of the circle that holds half of the possible places; the National SAR Supplement calls it the confidence factor, "normally 0.3", and Frost and Stone 2001, 4.6.1.3, report it and call it "perhaps optimistic")". Replace "Second, and **not yet checked against the source:** ... would be smaller (...)" up to "hours matter would stand" with "Second, checked against the sources: 0.3 is a probable error, not a radius that holds every dot, and the video's dots, all inside that radius, are simpler than the Coast Guard's spread. The Coast Guard adds the errors as a root sum of squares (E) and sizes its first search as a square of half-side 1.1 E, which holds about 65 in 100 of the spread (Frost and Stone 2001, Table 4-2 and 4.5.4); with the video's constants that first square gives 95, 73, 36 and 12 in 100 at 1, 3, 6 and 12 hours, and a circle that holds 95 in 100 of the spread gives 67, 37, 15 and 4. "Hours matter" stands." Close the decisions.md R2 "open:" item the same way, and add the two sources to the Sources list (Frost and Stone is there; add "United States National Search and Rescue Supplement to the IAMSAR Manual, 2000 edition, glossary"). Numbers in the replacement are mine and would need facts/oracle rows (F-D family) if kept.

title: Video H (bayesian_search): release: the verified final fetched and release-checked on the upload machine, uploaded Private for the owner's review, Public + MANIFEST + README row on the owner's word
description:
## Why

The finish line for Video H (`bayesian_search`): its verified 4K60 final on YouTube, Public, in the owner's channel, with its upload text, chapters, captions and thumbnail, and recorded. The four released videos had this as their ".16 release" bead (e.g. mx-e-a-8y5.16); E-K's epics stop at finals (mx-e-a-h-6ix2.11) and thumbnail + package (mx-e-a-h-6ix2.12), so nothing tracked the last step. Owner decisions that bind it (docs/publish/MANIFEST.md, 2026-10-12): voice `michael` for all; every cut is uploaded **Private for the owner's review first**; Public only on the owner's explicit word; only the upload lane (BronzeRidge, the owner's Codex session, from its own Chrome) uploads, edits metadata or changes visibility. Agents prepare and check; they never upload.

## Steps

1. Final verified on the build host (mx-e-a-h-6ix2.11 closed or its verify line `bayesian_search verify (<sha>) ... exit 0` in ~/jmev_orch/finals/status.log) and the delivery check posted on mx-e-a-h-6ix2.11 (final_check: ffprobe gates, loudness, chapter lengths, captions vs script; blank_stretches; band_dwell).
2. Upload text's chapter times filled from THIS final: `python3 -I tools/youtube_package.py fill bayesian_search --finals <scratch copy of the final's *.timeline.tsv>`, committed (a re-render moves starts: F v2 moved eight by 1-3 s).
3. On the laptop: `./x bayesian_search release-fetch --from mac-studio:<finals clone>` (brings master, SRT, VTT, timelines, thumbnail; preserves an older final as final_vN), then `./x bayesian_search release-check` -> PASS. Post its output (md5s, paths) on this bead.
4. Hand to the upload lane: MANIFEST "Ready, not uploaded" row from release-check's printed md5s (edited from the repo's current copy, never a stale copy), a note to BronzeRidge/GreenCarp with the paths.
5. Upload lane uploads Private: title.txt, description.txt, tags.txt, thumbnail, captions (English, the SRT), category Education, not made for kids, altered/synthetic content Yes (youtube.md's disclosure line). Record the link from Studio's state (Private, SD/HD/4K processed, SRT Published) in MANIFEST's Uploads table.
6. Owner reviews. If the owner asks for a fix: preserve the cut (final -> final_reviewN), fix, re-render, back to step 1 (new chapter times, new md5s). If the owner says Public: the upload lane flips it, MANIFEST row -> **Public** with the date, README's corpus row -> Published with the link and the measured length/LUFS (as rows 1-4).
7. GitHub Release asset for the cut: see the GitHub Releases bead (owner approval, G10).

## Done when

The video is Public at a youtu.be link recorded in MANIFEST with the master's md5, its README corpus row says Published with that link, and release-check PASSed on the exact master that was uploaded (its md5 equals MANIFEST's). Closed by the upload lane or GreenCarp with that evidence, not by the preparing agent.

title: Video J (matrix_exponential): release: the verified final fetched and release-checked on the upload machine, uploaded Private for the owner's review, Public + MANIFEST + README row on the owner's word
description:
## Why

The finish line for Video J (`matrix_exponential`): its verified 4K60 final on YouTube, Public, in the owner's channel, with its upload text, chapters, captions and thumbnail, and recorded. The four released videos had this as their ".16 release" bead (e.g. mx-e-a-8y5.16); E-K's epics stop at finals (mx-e-a-j-8yq7.10) and thumbnail + package (mx-e-a-j-8yq7.11), so nothing tracked the last step. Owner decisions that bind it (docs/publish/MANIFEST.md, 2026-10-12): voice `michael` for all; every cut is uploaded **Private for the owner's review first**; Public only on the owner's explicit word; only the upload lane (BronzeRidge, the owner's Codex session, from its own Chrome) uploads, edits metadata or changes visibility. Agents prepare and check; they never upload.

## Steps

1. Final verified on the build host (mx-e-a-j-8yq7.10 closed or its verify line `matrix_exponential verify (<sha>) ... exit 0` in ~/jmev_orch/finals/status.log) and the delivery check posted on mx-e-a-j-8yq7.10 (final_check: ffprobe gates, loudness, chapter lengths, captions vs script; blank_stretches; band_dwell).
2. Upload text's chapter times filled from THIS final: `python3 -I tools/youtube_package.py fill matrix_exponential --finals <scratch copy of the final's *.timeline.tsv>`, committed (a re-render moves starts: F v2 moved eight by 1-3 s).
3. On the laptop: `./x matrix_exponential release-fetch --from mac-studio:<finals clone>` (brings master, SRT, VTT, timelines, thumbnail; preserves an older final as final_vN), then `./x matrix_exponential release-check` -> PASS. Post its output (md5s, paths) on this bead.
4. Hand to the upload lane: MANIFEST "Ready, not uploaded" row from release-check's printed md5s (edited from the repo's current copy, never a stale copy), a note to BronzeRidge/GreenCarp with the paths.
5. Upload lane uploads Private: title.txt, description.txt, tags.txt, thumbnail, captions (English, the SRT), category Education, not made for kids, altered/synthetic content Yes (youtube.md's disclosure line). Record the link from Studio's state (Private, SD/HD/4K processed, SRT Published) in MANIFEST's Uploads table.
6. Owner reviews. If the owner asks for a fix: preserve the cut (final -> final_reviewN), fix, re-render, back to step 1 (new chapter times, new md5s). If the owner says Public: the upload lane flips it, MANIFEST row -> **Public** with the date, README's corpus row -> Published with the link and the measured length/LUFS (as rows 1-4).
7. GitHub Release asset for the cut: see the GitHub Releases bead (owner approval, G10).

## Done when

The video is Public at a youtu.be link recorded in MANIFEST with the master's md5, its README corpus row says Published with that link, and release-check PASSed on the exact master that was uploaded (its md5 equals MANIFEST's). Closed by the upload lane or GreenCarp with that evidence, not by the preparing agent.

comments.author: MaroonMarsh
comments.text:
CITATION CHECK, Video J (MaroonMarsh, read only; GrayCave/GoldenMountain hold the description, nothing edited). Asked by GreenCarp for the owner.

CLAIM. docs/description.md ~l.186-190: "use Krylov subspace methods or Chebyshev/Taylor action (`scipy.sparse.linalg.expm_multiply`, Al-Mohy and Higham 2011)". The Sources list has no 2011 entry (it has Higham 2005, Al-Mohy and Higham 2009, Estrada and Higham 2010), and docs/description_numbers.tsv row 2011 says "not in the fact sheet's source table nor in this file's Sources list (not verified here)".

SOURCE (seen). A. H. Al-Mohy and N. J. Higham, "Computing the Action of the Matrix Exponential, with an Application to Exponential Integrators", SIAM J. Sci. Comput. 33(2), 2011, pp. 488-511, DOI 10.1137/100788860. Read in the Manchester eprint (MIMS EPrint 2010.30, alhi11.pdf, which carries the published SISC first page and abstract); SciPy's docs page for expm_multiply and its source file _expm_multiply.py.
QUOTES. Abstract: "It uses the scaling part of the scaling and squaring method together with a truncated Taylor series approximation to the exponential." and "Experimental comparisons with MATLAB codes based on Krylov subspace, Chebyshev polynomial, and Laguerre polynomial methods show the new algorithm to be sometimes much superior in terms of computational cost and accuracy and accuracy." (the last 'and accuracy' once.) SciPy docs, References [1]: "Awad H. Al-Mohy and Nicholas J. Higham (2011) 'Computing the Action of the Matrix Exponential, with an Application to Exponential Integrators.' SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing, 33 (2). pp. 488-511". SciPy source: "This is algorithm (3.2) in Al-Mohy and Higham (2011)."

MATCH. Attribution of expm_multiply to this paper: correct (authors, year, journal, volume, pages as SciPy itself cites). Wording: loose. The paper's algorithm is a scaled, truncated Taylor series; Krylov and Chebyshev are the methods it is compared AGAINST, so putting "(expm_multiply, Al-Mohy and Higham 2011)" after "Krylov ... or Chebyshev/Taylor" credits the wrong method. Sources list: the entry is missing.

EXACT FIX.
1. Sources, add: "- Awad H. Al-Mohy and Nicholas J. Higham, "Computing the Action of the Matrix Exponential, with an Application to Exponential Integrators", *SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing* 33(2), 2011, pp. 488-511."
2. Replace "use Krylov subspace methods or Chebyshev/Taylor action (`scipy.sparse.linalg.expm_multiply`, Al-Mohy and Higham 2011)" with "use a Krylov subspace method, or a scaled, truncated Taylor series applied to the vector (`scipy.sparse.linalg.expm_multiply`, Al-Mohy and Higham 2011, who compare it with Krylov, Chebyshev and Laguerre codes)".
3. docs/fact-sheet.md source table: add the row (Seen: P, eprint + SciPy source); description_numbers.tsv 2011 row: the note "not verified here" can become "verified: SISC 33(2) 488-511".
Everything else J cites about Al-Mohy and Higham (2009, SIMAX 31(3) 970-989; the abstract of the 2011 paper itself cites it as the source of the error bounds) is consistent.

title: Epic Video G: Why Robot Arms Think in Lie Groups (lie_robotics)
description:
Produce Video G, working title "Why Robot Arms Think in Lie Groups", from the owner's request: "let's
make another video about the connection between Lie groups and robotics. Use the content from my
/dp/cmaes_explainer project, including the model of the Kuka robot arm and others you can find
online." and "Throughout the video, combine clear explanations, worked examples, and quizzes with
pauses before the answers." Robots: the KUKA LBR iiwa 14 R820 (every number from the xacro the
owner's project vendors, cited by path, never copied), the KMR iiwa mecanum base (planar motion,
SE(2)) and the Unitree G1 (a floating base in SE(3)). Arc: orientations do not add; rotations as a
group; why three angles fail; velocities and the exponential map; SE(2); SE(3) and screws; the arm as
a product of exponentials; the Jacobian, singularities and the seventh joint; inverse kinematics as
steps on the group; screw interpolation; the same mathematics elsewhere. This lane runs P0-P5
(brief, facts + oracle, storyboard + R1, script, build, drafts read as contact and cue sheets) and
stops for the owner; narration, score and 4K follow his review. Voice michael; 12-16 min; chapters
<= 85 s. Crate: explainer_corpus/lie_robotics.

title: Video G (lie_robotics): release: the verified final fetched and release-checked on the upload machine, uploaded Private for the owner's review, Public + MANIFEST + README row on the owner's word
description:
## Why

The finish line for Video G (`lie_robotics`): its verified 4K60 final on YouTube, Public, in the owner's channel, with its upload text, chapters, captions and thumbnail, and recorded. The four released videos had this as their ".16 release" bead (e.g. mx-e-a-8y5.16); E-K's epics stop at finals (mx-e-a-suh.11) and thumbnail + package (mx-e-a-suh.12), so nothing tracked the last step. Owner decisions that bind it (docs/publish/MANIFEST.md, 2026-10-12): voice `michael` for all; every cut is uploaded **Private for the owner's review first**; Public only on the owner's explicit word; only the upload lane (BronzeRidge, the owner's Codex session, from its own Chrome) uploads, edits metadata or changes visibility. Agents prepare and check; they never upload.

## Steps

1. Final verified on the build host (mx-e-a-suh.11 closed or its verify line `lie_robotics verify (<sha>) ... exit 0` in ~/jmev_orch/finals/status.log) and the delivery check posted on mx-e-a-suh.11 (final_check: ffprobe gates, loudness, chapter lengths, captions vs script; blank_stretches; band_dwell).
2. Upload text's chapter times filled from THIS final: `python3 -I tools/youtube_package.py fill lie_robotics --finals <scratch copy of the final's *.timeline.tsv>`, committed (a re-render moves starts: F v2 moved eight by 1-3 s).
3. On the laptop: `./x lie_robotics release-fetch --from mac-studio:<finals clone>` (brings master, SRT, VTT, timelines, thumbnail; preserves an older final as final_vN), then `./x lie_robotics release-check` -> PASS. Post its output (md5s, paths) on this bead.
4. Hand to the upload lane: MANIFEST "Ready, not uploaded" row from release-check's printed md5s (edited from the repo's current copy, never a stale copy), a note to BronzeRidge/GreenCarp with the paths.
5. Upload lane uploads Private: title.txt, description.txt, tags.txt, thumbnail, captions (English, the SRT), category Education, not made for kids, altered/synthetic content Yes (youtube.md's disclosure line). Record the link from Studio's state (Private, SD/HD/4K processed, SRT Published) in MANIFEST's Uploads table.
6. Owner reviews. If the owner asks for a fix: preserve the cut (final -> final_reviewN), fix, re-render, back to step 1 (new chapter times, new md5s). If the owner says Public: the upload lane flips it, MANIFEST row -> **Public** with the date, README's corpus row -> Published with the link and the measured length/LUFS (as rows 1-4).
7. GitHub Release asset for the cut: see the GitHub Releases bead (owner approval, G10).

## Done when

The video is Public at a youtu.be link recorded in MANIFEST with the master's md5, its README corpus row says Published with that link, and release-check PASSed on the exact master that was uploaded (its md5 equals MANIFEST's). Closed by the upload lane or GreenCarp with that evidence, not by the preparing agent.

title: Video B: fact sheet + oracle.py (P1)
description:
Fact sheet rows B-F1..B-F28 (plan §10.5); oracle.py reusing docs/research/raptorq_gf256/scripts (gf256np, rank_probs, toy_examples, misc_facts; measured counts pinned as recorded constants with their output file). Resolve the (to verify) items before narration: Erdos 1948 irrationality citation; RAID-6 Q = sum 2^i D_i in 0x11D and the 51-weight limit under 0x11B; QR codes' polynomial (285) against ISO/IEC 18004; whether RaptorQ (vs Raptor) is in 3GPP TS 26.346 (script says 'older sibling' until confirmed); Intel GFNI's polynomial (only if used).

Gate G1 (after the crate exists): `./x raptorq_gf256 facts-check` PASS (binary `facts` == oracle.py key by key; integers exact, others to 1e-9). Before the crate exists: oracle.py runs standalone with `python3 -I` and prints every value in the fact sheet.
Credit rules (AGENTS.md "Honest Credit"): real code and real tests in the same unit of work; no mocks or recorded fixtures presented as live proof; never weaken an assertion or regenerate a golden to get green; close only with evidence bound to a commit.
close_reason: Done at 9ebdf36: docs/facts/raptorq_gf256/{oracle.py,fact-sheet.md}. python3 -I oracle.py prints 297 keys in about 4 s, identical across runs; 22 internal cross-checks. All ledger rows B-F1..B-F28 match (spot-checked independently: 3*7=9, 2*128=29, 128*4=58, 150*3=167, 2*142=1, 0x57*0x83=0x31 under 0x11D, 0xC1 under 0x11B, ord 2 = 51 under 0x11B). Measured RaptorQ counts (B-F21 ablations, B-F22 Monte Carlo) are recorded constants, checked against their files in docs/research/raptorq_gf256/scripts/results/ on every run; B-F23 is quoted from RFC 6330 section 5.8. Open items: Erdos 1948 verified (the paper's theorem); RAID-6 verified (Anvin: 0x11D, g = {02}, '{02} is not a generator of the AES representation'); QR's 285 verified against ISO/IEC 18004:2006 clause 6.5.2 (2024 edition not checked); 3GPP TS 26.346 specifies Raptor (RFC 5053), not RaptorQ, so 'older sibling' stays; GFNI is unused by the script. Plan text corrected: element orders, 2 not a generator under AES's polynomial, 0.39215% exact. Caveat: the single 1-in-10^6 failure at K+2 cannot confirm the standard's requirement (95% CI 2.5e-8 to 5.6e-6); B-F18 / B-F25 Monte Carlo depend on CPython's RNG and must be pinned for G1.

title: explainer_kit: exact 8-bit colour via the P010 wire (ffmpeg writes the 8-bit stream)
description:
Found by spike S-5 (commit ae23be9). franken_manim's 8-bit NV12 wire is about 1.5 Cb codes short on dark blue. The corpus background #0E1116 is written as Y 30, Cb 129, Cr 126, where exact BT.709 limited-range codes are 30.37 / 130.50 / 126.48. The result is a slightly green-black background (#0D1112 on screen instead of #0E1116), visible under a contrast stretch and present in every 8-bit deliverable so far, v5's master included.

How it was measured:
- a CRF-0 (lossless) fmn render of a flat background, decoded to raw yuv420p;
- fmn's RGBA8 PNG frames are exact (14, 17, 22);
- fmn's P010 path writes 121 / 522 / 507, which is 130.5 x 4 for Cb, exact;
- ffmpeg's own RGB-to-yuv420p conversion writes 29 / 130 / 126.

The bias is introduced in fmn's fused NV12 conversion. fmn-frame's rgba_to_nv12 on the same pixels would round correctly.

Fix on the corpus side, without touching franken_manim: render on the P010 wire and let ffmpeg write the 8-bit H.264 stream. The kit's QualityRunner already rewrites the encode argv. It can replace fmn's `-pix_fmt yuv420p10le` (P010 in, 10-bit out) with `-pix_fmt yuv420p`, so swscale converts 10 to 8 bits with its rounding and dither, which also helps against banding. Set `file_writer.pixel_format = "p010le"` in delivery renders, including the CLI's options() after delivery_options.

Acceptance:
- A CRF-0 render of a flat #0E1116 frame decodes to Cb within 0.5 of 130.5 and Y within 0.5 of 30.37, against today's 129.
- The same check runs on a palette colour (Hoeffding yellow #FFD866).
- The 4K fps cost of the 2x pipe payload is measured (P010 is 25 MB per frame against NV12's 12 MB) and noted.
- The output stays 8-bit High profile H.264 with BT.709 tags; verify_video.sh passes.
- An integration test in the kit asserts the codes, with ffmpeg on PATH as the CLI tests already require.

Upstream: the same evidence goes into the franken_manim issue packet (U-18; filing needs the owner's OK).

Credit rules (AGENTS.md "Honest Credit"): real code and real tests in the same unit of work; no mocks or recorded fixtures presented as live proof; never weaken an assertion or regenerate a golden to get green; close only with evidence bound to a commit.
close_reason: Done at 3851db4, by a simpler fix than this bead proposed. The cause was not fmn's NV12 conversion. fmn's encode argv declares no colour space or range on its raw input (only on the output), so ffmpeg converts the frames from its default matrix. Exact NV12 bytes (30, 130, 126) fed through fmn's argv shape reproduce Cb 129, and come through exact once the input is tagged. The kit's runner now inserts -colorspace bt709 -color_range <output's> before -i - on raw-video jobs, and the NV12 wire stays (no 2x pipe payload, no P010). Acceptance: lossless (CRF 0) renders through the delivery encoder decode to background #0E1116 = 30/130/126 (BT.709 30.36/130.50/126.48) and yellow #FFD866 = 202/74/150 (201.56/74.00/149.72), all within 0.5 code (tests/exact_colour.rs). Planted negative: fmn's own argv gives background Cb 129 and yellow 203/75/146. Unit test for the argv (inserted once; mux jobs untouched); the VideoToolbox test restated to its intent (no rate control; only the input tags added). Output stays 8-bit High H.264 with BT.709 tags. The fps cost is none: the wire is unchanged.

title: explainer_kit: deterministic in-memory scene telemetry & invariant audit helpers (I-1..I-5)
description:
## Background & Motivation
Currently, individual explainer crates (`matrix_exponential`, `eigen_engineering`, `bayesian_search`, `lie_robotics`) have written local, ad-hoc test helpers (`draw::watch_dwell`, `marks.rs`, `QuizAudit`) to step chapters in-memory using the scratch voice (`run_voiced`) and inspect mobject visibility, dwell durations, and quiz countdown timing. However, `crates/explainer_kit` lacks a unified, reusable scene telemetry and invariant verification harness that all 11 explainers in `explainer_corpus/` can call from their `#[cfg(test)]` suites.

Several subtle `franken_manim` engine traps and 3Blue1Brown visual-continuity defects recur across videos and are expensive to discover only after 540p/4K renders and human montage reads:
1. **Retained-renderer `fade_in` point-count resize trap** (discovered in `eigen_engineering` `mx-e-a-e-k-oq4.7` `f63a276`): mutating a mobject's Bézier point count (`set_points`) while a `fade_in` animation is active freezes its opacity at ~0.02–0.06 for the rest of the scene.
2. **Premature quiz answer reveals or sub-second post-reveal flashes** (`REVIEW-AND-CONTINUITY.md` §5): quiz answers appearing before the countdown ring hits zero, or cards fading out <1.0 s after reveal as the next spoken line begins.
3. **Lower-third reading-rate starvation**: `"precisely:"`, `"for programmers:"`, or `"who and when:"` bands appearing late in a spoken line and getting wiped <2.5 s later by the next beat.
4. **Black-stage seams between beats**: sequential `fade_out` followed by `fade_in` (instead of overlapped crossfade or `hand_over`) leaving the stage empty for 0.5–7.0 s under spoken narration.
5. **Collinear polygon collapse on 2D reflections**: linear point interpolation across a mirror axis collapsing polygon area to zero at midpoint `e = 0.5`.

## Mathematical & Technical Specification (Invariants I-1..I-5)
Stepping a chapter scene at 10–15 fps in-memory (`stage.scene_mut()` without pixel rasterization or FFmpeg encoding) takes <0.5 s in `cargo test` and allows every chapter to prove five deterministic invariants:

1. **Invariant I-1 — Bézier Point-Count Stability Under Opacity Transitions:**
   For every mobject `m` in the scene arena at consecutive sampled frames `t_{k-1}, t_k`:
   If `|alpha_m(t_k) - alpha_m(t_{k-1})| > 1e-4` and `0.01 < alpha_m(t_k) < 0.99` (i.e. `m` is actively fading in or out), then `points_m(t_k).len() == points_m(t_{k-1}).len()`.
2. **Invariant I-2 — Causal Quiz Masking & Post-Zero Answer Dwell:**
   For every registered quiz with countdown window `[t_ring, t_zero]`:
   - Answer mobjects satisfy `alpha_ans(t) == 0` for all `t < t_zero - 1/fps`.
   - Within `0.5 s` after `t_zero`, `alpha_ans(t) >= 0.95`.
   - The answer remains on-scene with `alpha_ans(t) >= 0.90` for `dwell >= max(1.5 s, W_ans / 3.5 wps)` (and until the first spoken sentence after the countdown completes).
3. **Invariant I-3 — Lower-Third Legibility & Reading-Rate Gate:**
   Every lower-third with word count `W` remains on-scene at `alpha >= 0.90` for `dwell >= max(2.5 s, W / 4.0 wps)` and stays within the lower-third vertical band (`y in [-3.85, -2.85]`) with zero bounding-box intersection against stage content (`y > -2.75`).
4. **Invariant I-4 — Non-Empty Stage Under Spoken Narration:**
   For every spoken line `L_i` spanning `[t_start, t_end]`, over `[t_start + 0.6 s, t_end - 0.3 s]`, the total visible non-backdrop bounding-box area satisfies `sum_{m notin Backdrop} alpha_m(t) * Area(bbox(m)) > 0.25 stage units^2`.
5. **Invariant I-5 — Non-Collinear Reflection Morph Area Gate:**
   Provide a shared geometric helper/assertion verifying that any reflected polygon morph maintains shoelace area `|A(e)| >= A_min > 0` across all `e in [0, 1]` via out-of-line normal bulge `b * sin(pi * e) * n_perp` and midpoint guard `|e - 0.5| < 0.01`.

## Files to Touch
- `crates/explainer_kit/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/explainer_kit/src/lint.rs` (or a new `crates/explainer_kit/src/telemetry.rs` module exported from `lib.rs`)

## Verification & Testing Requirements
- Unit tests in `crates/explainer_kit` exercising synthetic passing and failing scenes for each invariant (I-1 through I-5), verifying that each failure produces a structured diagnostic (`chapter`, `line_id`, `scene_time_s`, `mob_label`, `expected`, `actual`).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` in `crates/explainer_kit`, and `ubs` clean.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Shared telemetry/audit module in crates/explainer_kit steps chapter scenes in-memory without pixel rasterization or FFmpeg encoding (<0.5s per chapter). 2. Enforces Invariant I-1 (Bezier point-count stability under opacity transitions), Invariant I-2 (causal quiz masking & post-zero dwell), Invariant I-3 (lower-third legibility & reading-rate gate), Invariant I-4 (non-empty stage under spoken narration), and Invariant I-5 (non-collinear reflection morph area check). 3. Emits structured failure diagnostics (chapter, line_id, scene_time_s, mob_label, expected, actual). 4. Unit tests in explainer_kit pass cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings.
close_reason: Landed commit 787fef2: added crates/explainer_kit/src/telemetry.rs (re-exported in lib.rs) with SceneFrame, SceneRecorder, InvariantDiagnostic, guard_reflection_param, normal_bulge_offset, shoelace_area, and deterministic invariant checkers I-1..I-5. Verified on build host: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -p explainer_kit --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test -p explainer_kit --lib (76/76 pass including planted-negative unit and live headless run_scene tests), ubs Critical 0.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Refinement Round 1 (Technical Architecture & API Specification):
- In crates/explainer_kit/src/lint.rs (or telemetry.rs), provide a headless scene stepper (e.g. SceneTelemetry::record(stage, fps)) that samples stage.scene() at each frame step during scratch-voice or timeline-backed test runs.
- At each sampled frame k (time t_k = k / fps), record per-MobjectId snapshots: (opacity, points.len(), bounding_box, is_backdrop, tag/role).
- Invariant I-1 (fade_in/fade_out point-count stability): if (opacity_k - opacity_{k-1}).abs() > 1e-4 and 0.01 < opacity_k < 0.99, assert points_len_k == points_len_{k-1}. This catches the exact franken_manim retained-renderer defect encountered in eigen_engineering (f63a276) where mutating a truss polygon's vertex count mid-fade froze its alpha at ~0.04.
- Invariant I-2 (quiz reveal causality & post-zero dwell): for each QuizWindow { line_id, ring_start_s, ring_zero_s, first_sentence_after_s, answer_mobs, word_count }, assert max opacity of answer_mobs is 0.0 for all t < ring_zero_s - 1.0/fps, reaches >= 0.95 within 0.5 s after ring_zero_s, and stays >= 0.90 until max(ring_zero_s + max(1.5, word_count as f64 / 3.5), first_sentence_after_s - 0.05).
- Invariant I-3 (lower-third reading-rate & band clearance): for each LowerThirdWindow { line_id, mob_id, word_count }, assert full-opacity dwell (opacity >= 0.90) is >= max(2.5, word_count as f64 / 4.0) s, bbox.y_min >= -3.85, bbox.y_max <= -2.85, and zero bbox intersection with non-backdrop stage mobjects above y = -2.75.
- Invariant I-4 (non-empty stage under speech): for each spoken line [t_start, t_end], over [t_start + 0.6, t_end - 0.3], assert sum of alpha_m * area(bbox_m) for non-backdrop mobjects > 0.25 stage units^2.

title: Epic W2: explainer_score, the warm procedural sound engine
description:

title: explainer_score: PolyBLEP oscillators, OU drift, TPT/SVF/ZDF ladder, FIR, DC blocker
description:
Implement (formulas in docs/research/sound_design/MEMO.md §3.1-3.2; Zavalishin VA filter design): PolyBLEP saw/pulse (PWM)/triangle (leaky-integrated square), sine, white and pink noise; Ornstein-Uhlenbeck pitch drift in cents (theta 0.5-1 /s, stationary spread 2-4 cents); TPT one-pole, Simper SVF (low/band/high), 4-pole ZDF ladder with exact zero-delay solve, ADAA tanh in the loop and passband compensation; RBJ biquads; linear-phase FIR designer (windowed sinc, 1,023 taps); DC blocker. title: explainer_score: timeline, offline VAD, duck curves and the speech pocket
description:

Plan §7.2; memo §2.3. Never franken_manim's gain_to_background (a step gain on the whole mix, no ramps, insertion order).

Tests: duck curve continuous and monotone on each ramp; exact region boundaries for a synthetic timeline; pocket FIR response within +-0.5 dB of spec; an authored music_breath of 2.5 s yields an undecked window; listen windows (>= 3 s) release the duck fully.
Credit rules (AGENTS.md "Honest Credit"): real code and real tests in the same unit of work; no mocks or recorded fixtures presented as live proof; never weaken an assertion or regenerate a golden to get green; close only with evidence bound to a commit.

title: explainer_score: score DSL, buses and stem render (two-pass, per act, sliced per chapter)
description:
Score DSL (plan §7.4-7.5): Identity (key, mode, tempo with +-8% elastic phrasing, palette, leitmotif in scale degrees, seed) and ChapterPlan (harmony with chords of 4-16 s changing only in gaps or intra-sentence pauses >= 0.2 s and never within 150 ms of a speech onset; an intensity arc 0..1 driving density, cutoff, register spread and reverb send; cues anchored to line ids, marks and listen windows; cue types: reveal stinger, transition swell, aha resolution, tick/counter, pizzicato count, whoosh/riser, sonification). Mixer: buses (bed, colour, cue, sfx) -> sends -> duck + pocket -> stem; music stem true peak <= -12 dBTP. Two-pass (D-22): render each act (or the whole video) from the combined timeline, then slice at frame-aligned sample boundaries into stems/<chapter>.music.f32.wav, each exactly its scene's length. Cache by hash of (identity, plan, timeline, narration WAV digests, crate version). Hard rules 4-8 of §7.3 enforced (attacks, cue density, no identical buffer within 10 s via round-robin + seeded micro-variation, pentagon-safe cue pitches, no melodic phrase starting under speech).

Tests: determinism (same inputs, same bytes on one platform); chapter independence (editing chapter k's plan leaves other chapters' stem fingerprints unchanged within +-0.5 dB per third-octave per second); slices concatenate to the act render exactly; stem length == scene samples.
Credit rules (AGENTS.md "Honest Credit"): real code and real tests in the same unit of work; no mocks or recorded fixtures presented as live proof; never weaken an assertion or regenerate a golden to get green; close only with evidence bound to a commit.

title: explainer_score: score QA metrics + JSON report; hard-rule violations fail the render
description:
Plan §7.6 metrics per chapter, computed offline from the voice bus (placed narration) and the music stem: voice-music short-term loudness over speech (median >= 16 LU, p5 >= 12 LU); music's loudest 400 ms during speech <= speech's loudest 400 ms - 15 LU; SII-lite loss per 400 ms (third-octave bands, ANSI S3.5 band-importance weights) median <= 0.01, max <= 0.03; music/voice band ratio 1-4 kHz during speech <= -20 dB; stem true peak <= -12 dBTP; click detector (onset energy > 8 kHz) 0 flags; monotony (>= 1 chord change per 16 s; no 8 s segment repeated > 3x at correlation > 0.98); busyness (<= 2 onsets/s under speech, <= 6 in gaps); roughness from the score (no sustained partial pair 15-60 Hz apart both above -20 dB); mono compatibility (L/R correlation >= 0 per 3 s); sanity (no NaN/inf, DC <= -60 dBFS, exact length). `./x <slug> score` fails on any violation and writes the JSON report.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Candidate U-18 (evidence for the owner, not filed): fmn's 8-bit NV12 wire biases chroma. Repro at e2eec632: render a flat #0E1116 background with x264 CRF 0 (lossless), decode to yuv420p: Y 30, Cb 129, Cr 126; exact BT.709 limited codes are 30.37/130.50/126.48 (Cb 1.5 codes low: blue lost, background reads green-black). fmn's RGBA8 frames are exact (PNG 14,17,22), fmn-frame::rgba_to_nv12's quant8 rounds correctly (it would write 130), and the P010 path writes 121/522/507 (exact); so the bias is in the renderer's fused NV12 conversion. Also from S-5: U-16 (camera-route MP4 with audio untested) now has a passing render through the kit's wrapper (AAC muxed, durations equal).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Correction to candidate U-18 (3851db4): the cause is in fmn-output/src/negotiate.rs encode_argv, which tags the output (-colorspace bt709 -color_range tv) but not the rawvideo input, so ffmpeg converts from its default matrix. The NV12 conversion itself is exact: NV12 bytes 30/130/126 through that argv shape decode as Cb 129, and through it with '-colorspace bt709 -color_range tv' before '-i -' they decode exact. Impact at e2eec632, lossless: #0E1116 Cb 130.5 -> 129; #FFD866 Cr 149.7 -> 146, Y 201.6 -> 203. Suggested upstream fix: emit the input's colour description in encode_argv. The corpus works around it in its runner.

title: GitHub Releases for the published cuts (plan D-12; zero exist): bundles out of the tracked tree, thumbnail in the bundle, upload on the owner's word
description:
## Why

The plan (docs/planning/COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_JEFFS_MATH_EXPLAINER_VIDEOS.md D-12, line ~599: "GitHub Release assets, one release per video version"), AGENTS.md ("Finished cuts ship as GitHub Release assets, and only with the owner's approval") and README ("Renders never enter git; finished cuts ship as GitHub Release assets") all promise it. `gh release list` on Dicklesworthstone/jeffs_math_explainer_videos returns nothing (checked 2026-10-14 14:45): zero releases. The A-D release beads (mx-e-a-8y5.16 and its siblings for B, C and Hoeffding) named "GitHub Release <slug>-v1" in scope and were closed on YouTube publication without one. The masters fit GitHub's 2 GB asset limit (A-D: 68-461 MB; F v2 84 MB).

## What

1. publish.py writes its bundle into the tracked tree (`explainer_corpus/<slug>/publish/release_vN/`, not gitignored): move the default to `renders/release_vN/` (ignored) or add `explainer_corpus/*/publish/release_*/` to .gitignore, so a 4K MP4 can never be staged by a pathspec slip. Add the thumbnail PNG to the bundle and its line to release_notes.md.
2. Assemble bundles (dry run, no approval needed) for the four Public cuts from the exact masters MANIFEST names (md5 checked against MANIFEST before assembling), then for each E-K cut as it goes Public.
3. Ask the owner once (through GreenCarp/BronzeRidge) for the go; on it, `ALLOW_PUBLISH_UPLOAD=1 ./x <slug> publish --upload` per video (tag `<slug>-vN`, the master, the 1080p proxy, SRT/VTT, contact sheet, release notes, SHA256SUMS). Record each release URL in MANIFEST.
4. Comment on the closed A-D release beads that the GitHub Release part was not done and is tracked here (honest record, no reopen churn).

## Tests

test_driver.py publish test: the bundle lands in an ignored path (`git check-ignore` on it), includes the thumbnail, release_notes names it; md5 mismatch against MANIFEST refuses. Owner gate: `--upload` without ALLOW_PUBLISH_UPLOAD=1 still exits 2 (existing test).

title: Narration: line gaps from the thought instead of the constant 0.6 s BREATH (kit)
description: Owner 2026-10-14: 'bizarre pauses'. comments.author: EmeraldOwl
comments.text:
Landed 34bbcfa (pushed to origin/main): LineGaps::Thought in crates/explainer_kit/src/narration.rs, opt-in per video through the new Explainer.line_gaps field (every video, the kit tests and the example set Constant; Video F is NOT opted in until the owner's A/B; mental_math has a test that pins that and says to update it when he decides).
What it does: classify_gap(prev, next) from the two lines' text (Topic: next opens with Your turn / Take / Here's / Last one / One more / Most / The next, on a word boundary; Continuation: next opens with And/But/So/Then/Now/Because/Which/Plus/Or/That's, or the line before ends unfinished (a closing quote or bracket after the end mark does not hide the end); Beat: the rest); gap = audible silence 0.58 / 0.81 / 0.99 s (T-007 + P-4 human numbers) minus the two takes' own quiet edges (quiet_edges: T-007's detector, measured at load from the WAVs only under Thought), floor 0.10 s. A chapter's first line is placed by the class of the pair across the chapter join, from its lead only (Script::select keeps the full script, so a partial render opens where the whole render does). Authored windows (music_breath, listen, sonify) keep their length and their breath; hold never waits longer than BREATH, so whatever an author puts after a hold keeps its place (a continuation shortens it to 0.58 s). Cue waits keyed to a line's start or end (said_at, sentence_at, length) move with the lines by construction; the one BREATH constant outside the kit (mental_math bethe.rs, a wait up to a listen window) is keyed to the window, which keeps BREATH, so it stays right. check_gap_spread/gap_cv/MIN_GAP_CV=0.10 is the QA: Video F's plain gaps varied by about 0.04 under the constant rule, the classes on its real script by 0.16.
Tests (all new, real code): unit tests in narration.rs: classification table with planted negatives (a connective is the whole first word, an opener is a phrase not a prefix), quiet_edges on synthetic takes at 24 and 48 kHz with negatives (no silence, a 30 ms lead under the 40 ms run, silence only, shorter than a frame, a soft word 12 dB under the voice is not silence), line_gap/gap_before with real WAV takes (class minus tail minus lead, the floor, the constant rule ignoring text, window/first-line/video-first-line states), partial render equals whole render, constant gaps fail the spread check. Integration (tests/narrated_scene.rs): a frame-exact narrated scene under both rules (Constant reproduces the old placement 36/87/138/189/300, windows at 240; Thought 36/86/150/225/336, window 276, the line after it exactly 60 frames later in both), and a chapter rendered alone against the whole (60 vs 36 frames). mental_math: the ten plain pairs of ch 02 and 07 get the classes the P-4 pilot built (BEAT 02_1>2, 02_7>8, 07_1>2; CONT 02_2>3, 02_3>4, 02_5>6, 02_8>9; TOPIC 07_2>3, 07_4>5, 07_5>6), the 13 chapter joins open as all three classes, planned gaps of the whole script pass the spread check and constant BREATH fails it. Mutation check: removing the hold's min(BREATH) fails the integration test ([86,150] against [86,137]).
Gates, run on the build host in a private scratch tree (laptop tree rsynced, peers' dirty explainer_score/score files back at HEAD, own CARGO_TARGET_DIR): cargo fmt -p explainer_kit -p mental_math_explainer --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- D warnings Finished (kit, score and all 11 video crates); cargo test -p explainer_kit: lib 69 passed (55 before, 14 new) and every integration test ok, incl. narrated_scene 8/8; cargo test -p mental_math_explainer 36 passed; ubs on the 5 files I changed in substance: exit 0, 0 critical (warnings +85, almost all unwrap/assert in the new tests; two real ones fixed: direct indexing in opens_with and quiet_edges). cargo fmt --all --check shows one diff in crates/explainer_score/src/qa.rs, a peer's dirty file, not mine.
Not done / open: (1) the chapter tail is still the video's own constant (mental_math END_HOLD_S via music_breath), so only the lead of a chapter varies with the class (0.58 / 0.81 / 0.99 s less the lead, instead of the constant 0.6 s): joins that were ten copies of 3.52 s become 3.3-3.9 s; varying the tail is video code. (2) hold now stops short of a beat or a topic (it waits at most BREATH), so the picture's wipe can precede the next line's voice by up to 0.4 s of empty stage; if the owner dislikes that, hold can wait the full class gap at the cost of shifting an authored window that follows it. (3) in-line sentence gaps (the P-1 question) are narration assembly in tools/narration.py, not this bead. (4) no render or listening: the owner's A/B decides; to turn it on set Explainer.line_gaps to LineGaps::Thought in a video's main.rs and update the mental_math pin test.

comments.text:
Independent review of 34bbcfa (GrayCave, pane 7; I did not write or edit any of it). VERIFIED, with three non-blocking test/QA findings. Everything below was run on the build host from clean `git archive` exports of 34bbcfa and of its parent (no .git, own target dir); evidence kept outside the repo.

VERIFIED
1. Tests re-run on the clean export of 34bbcfa: cargo test -p explainer_kit: lib 69 passed, narrated_scene 8/8, camera_chapter, cli_pipeline 3/3, exact_colour, glyph_probe 3/3, layout_scene, scene_smoke, stems_decode, two_route_segments all ok. cargo test -p mental_math_explainer: 36 passed, incl. the_thought_classes_of_the_real_script_follow_the_thought. cargo check --workspace --all-targets: all 11 video crates + kit + score build (rc 0). cargo clippy -p explainer_kit --all-targets -D warnings: rc 0. rustfmt --check on the 19 changed .rs files: no diff in any line the commit touched (explainer_corpus/hoeffding_d/src/main.rs has 6 older diffs, identical in the parent). tools/scan_private.sh on the changed files: clean.
2. LineGaps::Constant leaves every timeline byte-identical. Built the `mental` binary from the parent and from 34bbcfa and ran `render all --timeline-only --narration <F's 88 chosen takes>` with each: timeline.tsv, cues.tsv and cuelog.tsv are md5-identical for all 14 chapters (42 of 42 files). Chapter 02 timeline.tsv c8f76187665447d8130cc9d5cd3f3f70 before and after; chapter 07 311e4d9489dfe18240fdbda91335c789 before and after.
3. The negatives are real: 18 mutants of narration.rs, each applied alone to the clean export and tested. 16 killed, by the test the author named or another: say ignores the class; gap_before and line_gap ignoring Constant (also killed by the pre-existing frame-exact test the_narrator_places_lines_frame_exactly..., so the off-rule is pinned twice); Constant +20 ms; hold never following the class; hold without .min(BREATH) ([86,150] vs [86,137], as the author said); window() forgetting After::Window; select dropping the lines before the selection; MIN_GAP_CV 0 (constant-gap negative stops failing); quiet_edges returning no edges; no connectives; "Take " removed from the topic openers (both of the last two are also killed by F's real-script test alone: 02_2->02_3 Beat for Continuation, 07_4->07_5 Beat for Topic); no MIN_GAP_S floor; chapter-first line taking a tail; edges measured under Constant; Continuation/Beat durations swapped.
4. Real takes, not just synthetic: with a scratch copy of F's main.rs set to Thought (not committed), chapters 02 and 07 rendered alone give timeline/cues/cuelog md5-identical to the same chapters in the whole render (partial = whole on the real binary). Authored windows unchanged: the line after every listen/breath starts exactly where it did (0.0 s or 0.6 s after the window end, 14 chapters). 37 of the 45 plain joins moved; the other 8 are set by the scene's own picture waits. Total chapter time 936.0 -> 941.1 s (+0.55%). Detected silence (T-007/P-4 detector over the assembled voice track), median: Continuation 0.63 (class 0.58), Beat 0.835 (0.81), Topic 1.03 (0.99). Chapter joins (tail + next lead, voice only): ten were 3.52-3.53 s; now 12 distinct values 3.45-5.78 s (median 3.53 -> 3.82), as the author said (his "3.3-3.9" is 3.45-4.24 on the real takes, plus the 5.78 outlier).

FINDINGS (none blocks the landing; Video F stays on Constant)
F1 test gap, two behaviours no test covers (mutants survive the whole kit suite and F's tests, and are NOT equivalent: shown on the real binary). (a) listen() setting After::Window (the quiz countdown: all 20 of F's listen windows): remove it and the line after the window in 03_your_turn starts 4 frames late (756 -> 760) under Thought; the test only uses music_breath (window()). (b) reset() clearing After: remove it and, rendering 02,03,04 in one run, 03 and 04 open 24 and 21 frames early (60 -> 36, 57 -> 36) because the first line takes the previous chapter's last line's tail. Suggest: a Thought scene with kit.sonify/listen followed by a line (starts exactly at the window end), and one Narrator rendered over two chapters with reset() between (second chapter's first line equals the partial render).
F2 check_gap_spread is not a QA over a real timeline. Nothing calls it outside tests, and the planted negatives are synthetic lists ([0.69, 0.70, ...], [0.6; 8]). Applied to F's real constant-rule timeline it passes unless authored/picture waits are excluded: every pair with no window row between (n=52, includes the 2.6 s prediction pauses and 1.5 s picture waits) CV 0.716 -> PASS; only the 45 pairs under 1.0 s (T-008's "plain") give CV 0.039 -> FAIL as designed (Thought: 0.217). When this is wired to a gate it needs that definition of plain; the commit text "check_gap_spread is the QA" overstates it today.
F3 "heard as the class (to within a frame)" (quiet_edges doc, commit message) holds for the synthetic takes only. On F's real takes the detected silence is +0.05 / +0.025 / +0.04 s over the class in median, 15 of 45 joins more than 0.05 s off, and 0.02-0.09 s longer than the P-4 pack's `g` files the owner will compare (mean +0.05 s): the kit takes each take's own p95 as the reference, the human numbers were measured against the recording's. Perceptually small; the wording should say about 0.1 s.
Notes, not findings: Thought changes a chapter's tail only through `hold` (reads the next chapter's first line when the last line is held); F's chapters end in music_breath, so none changes. Narration is untouched by the commit (kit timeline only). The in-line sentence gaps (P-1) are not in this bead, as the author said.

title: Upload text numbers: tools/youtube_package.py check holds every number in description.txt/title.txt to docs/description.md or script.tsv
description:
## Why

The project's promise is that every number a viewer sees is computed and oracle-checked (README badge "every number: oracle-checked"; docs/description.md's numbers are bound to facts by tools/description_numbers.py and docs/description_numbers.tsv). The YouTube description is the one place a viewer reads numbers that no check covers. Observed 2026-10-14: the first E package (73112bd's youtube.md text) said "matches occur 68% of the time, so on average it takes 6.25 tosses (or 3.125 pairs)" and "Knuth-Yao achieve optimal entropy extraction rates": "68%" and "3.125" stand nowhere in docs/description.md (68.5% is the dice figure; 3.125 is an oracle key but not a sentence of the notes). The lanes that cut G and H checked their numbers by hand ("its 19 numbers all stand in docs/description.md").

## What

In tools/youtube_package.py `check`: every number token in description.txt and title.txt (digits with optional separators, decimals, percent, signs, unicode minus; excluding the chapter lines' M:SS times, the URL, and years inside a Sources line) must occur as a token in docs/description.md or script.tsv's text (normalized: thousands separators and unicode minus folded). One line per missing number with its context. Skip when the video has no docs/description.md (A-D's packages predate it: confirm they still pass or record why not).

## Tests

test_youtube_package.py: a number present in the notes passes; "68%" absent fails naming it; "3,125" vs "3125" and "−1" vs "-1" fold; a chapter time "1:05" and the GitHub URL's digits are not numbers; a year in the Sources block is skipped; old-code run fails the new test. Run over all eleven packages and post the result (expect E-K PASS on numbers; fix or report any that fail).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Built and pushed in f3977ee (CloudyFinch). Opt-in per video: Identity::steady_bed, false in all eight identities.

What it does: the bed bus stays duck_db down in the pocket's tone for the whole video (duck::apply_held), is kept to its median level under speech + 0.5 dB wherever the voice is not (duck::ceiling: a smooth gain from the 400 ms loudness, never inside speech), and a join the next chapter starts more than 1 dB under is carried by bringing the end of the last chapter down (duck::carry). A listen window's sonification is not part of the bed: it keeps today's duck curve and today's level, so listen_lu (F: -10) is the tick-level parameter and is untouched; the owner decides it.
QA: bed_swell_db and join_step_db are reported for every score, judged (3 LU / 1.5 LU) only for a steady one; `clicks` is not counted inside a steady score's sonified windows (the bed has nothing above 2.5 kHz to hide a mallet strike in; 8 of 14 chapters failed it on the countdown ticks before that).

comments.author: EmeraldOwl
comments.text:
APPROVE the loosening, with one non-blocking weakness (independent review of CloudyFinch's 877263b, the steady bed's join limit 1.5 -> 3.5 LU and the silence-return exclusion; EmeraldOwl, read only). Method: clean export of origin/main at 877263b (HEAD's identities have steady_bed on, a4aff0e); each of the seven videos scored with its own binary, `score --timelines <copy of the studio's renders/timeline>`, into a scratch out dir; the joins read from the written chapter stems with the crate's own meter::join_step_db (400 ms momentary windows, median 0.2 to 1.5 s after minus before), raw and as Score::join_step_db reads them; crate tests 161 pass.

1. Every join step of the seven videos (92 joins; 91 readable): |step| median 0.89, 95th percentile 1.88, largest 3.32 among the ones QA reads, and one hidden (K 04 -> 05, raw +6.64, below). QA passes all chapters of all seven except J 14 (the studio's pre-fix timeline, the open silence of 52faab0). Video I on the same timelines with the score code from before 52faab0/877263b fails QA in 04 and 07 (the old 1.5 limit) and passes now; its 15 chapter stems are byte-identical either way.

2. The ten joins with 1.5 <= |step| <= 3.5 (raw = QA, none hidden), with the voice's share of the 1.5 s either side and the bed's level either side: I 03 -> 04 +1.83 (speech 42% / 57%; bed -44.4 -> -42.7 LUFS); I 06 -> 07 -3.32 (59% / 59%; -40.9 -> -44.1); G 01 -> 02 -1.83 (59 / 54; -41.3 -> -43.2); G 03 -> 04 +2.35 (55 / 60; -42.6 -> -40.2); G 08 -> 09 -2.56 (59 / 59; -40.6 -> -43.2); G 11 -> 12 +1.91 (56 / 59; -43.7 -> -41.8); E 01 -> 02 +1.60 (0 / 60; -45.0 -> -42.7); E 07 -> 08 +1.68 (0 / 60; -42.2 -> -40.6); E 08 -> 09 +1.88 (0 / 60; -42.2 -> -40.3); H 04 -> 05 -1.58 (58 / 57; -41.6 -> -44.0). F, J and K have none in that band. Over the voice, which sits about 18 LU above the bed, the largest (I 06 -> 07) is a 3.3 LU drop of a bed at -41 LUFS while the narrator speaks; E's three are rises of 1.6 to 1.9 LU after 1.5 s with no voice (music alone before, voice after). I cannot say what the owner hears from numbers; these are the joins to listen to. The margin is thin where it matters: 3.32 against 3.5 (0.18 LU), on timelines that the finals' re-narration will move.

3. Can the silence-return exclusion swallow a real step? It can; today it did not. Rule: a join is not read when any authored silence has fade_start < join + 1.7 s and back_end > join - 1.7 s. In the seven videos two joins are excluded: I 14 -> 15 (silence:cross, closed: fade out 19.3 s before the join, back 0.6 s before, back_end 0.9 s after; the stem is zero there, so even the raw reading is None) and K 04 -> 05 (silence:closing_sentence, unterminated: back 1.4 s before, back_end 0.1 s after; the raw +6.64 is the music coming back, which is what 877263b meant to stop reading). The step across each silence (the bed's median level 0.2 to 1.7 s after the return finished minus 0.2 to 1.7 s before the silence began): I +0.64 LU, K -1.43 LU, so no real step was hidden. Planted: +6 dB added to K's stem from chapter 05 on: raw +12.64, QA None (the step across the silence +4.57 LU): swallowed; the same +6 dB at I's 08 -> 09, a join with no silence near, reads +6.21 and would fail the limit. The exclusion is wholesale: it also drops a join whose 'before' windows (1.5 to 0.2 s before) are clean because the return finished 1.5 s ahead, and one where only a few of the 13 windows touch the return. Suggested, not required: where a silence is near, judge the step across it (levels after back_end and before fade_start) against the same 3.5 instead of returning None; today's two values (+0.64, -1.43) would pass.

4. For CloudyFinch's up-carry: the limit should come down only on a re-score of the finals, not these timelines: the 91 steps above are the data, and 3.32 and the ten steps in 1.5 to 3.5 are what a lower limit would have to carry away.

It checks what verify_video.sh does not: the master against the EXPECT gates (3840x2160, 60 fps, BT.709 primaries/transfer/matrix, A/V delta <= 0.2 s), its own EBU R128 (-16 +-1 LUFS or the recorded fixed-gain exception, true peak <= -1.0 dBTP), each chapter's size/fps/length vs its timeline and the 85 s limit, and the SRT against script.tsv word for word (spelled numbers, lexicon respellings, <= 2 lines x 42 chars, cue boundaries on sentence boundaries, inside each line's audio, VTT = SRT); deliver.sh adds tools/blank_stretches.py and tools/band_dwell.py. It found F v1's orphan captions and 07's 87.6 s chapter. It lives only in build-host scratch: not in git, not reviewable, not runnable by another lane or on another machine, and lost if the host loses its home scratch (the host already lost /tmp once, 2026-10-12). This is finished code not wired in.

## What

- `tools/final_check.py`: the scratch script moved into the repo with its author's knowledge (EmeraldOwl), behaviour unchanged except: `--strict` exits 1 when any DEFECT line was printed (default stays a reader, exit 0); the skill path for narration helpers stays a flag with the current default; no hard-coded home paths beyond defaults.
- `./x <slug> final-check [--clone DIR]` runs final_check + blank_stretches + band_dwell niced, like deliver.sh, printing to stdout (deliver.sh's log file becomes the caller's redirect).
- release-check (tools/release.py) runs `final_check --strict --no-loudness` on the fetched final when present (loudness needs the full decode; it is the build host's job and its result is on the .11 bead).

## Tests

tools/test_final_check.py on a fixture final in a temp root (script.tsv with three lines, a report.json, SRT/VTT, timelines; ffprobe and ebur128 injected): PASS on the fixture; planted negatives each produce exactly one DEFECT: a caption word missing, a three-line cue, a 43-character line, a cue crossing a sentence boundary, VTT text differing from SRT, a chapter longer than 85 s, a chapter 0.5 s off its timeline, A/V delta 0.3 s, 1920x1080 master; `--strict` exit 1 on each, 0 on the fixture. E2E: `./x mental_math final-check --clone ~/projects/jeffs_math_explainer_videos_finals2` on mac-studio reproduces the v2 result posted on mx-e-a-f-ms4.11 (no orphans, -18.1 LUFS, 07 87.6 s).

## Coordination

The script is EmeraldOwl's; ask on this bead before moving it, keep its history in the commit message (where it ran, what it found), and leave the scratch copy in place until EmeraldOwl switches.

Independent review of tools/description_numbers.py (dde0c05) by GrayCave, pane 7, written while checking the G, H, I and K description audits. The tool does what its header says (its 16 tests pass on a clean export, and it flagged nothing on the four descriptions after the audits); what it can promise is narrower than 'every number is a fact':
1. Matching is key-blind: a number passes if any number in any oracle value agrees. With 190 to 330 oracle lines per video, almost every small count is some value's number. Counting how many of each description's fact-matched numbers would still pass if changed by one unit (last digit): small whole numbers G 210/229, H 118/123, I 232/248, K 238/261 (91 to 96%); numbers with a point, a % or 100+ G 24/108, H 57/119, I 4/35, K 91/216.
2. Planted single-number errors, one at a time, in the real descriptions (17 plants): 12 were NOT caught: G rank 5 -> 4, bend 21.5 -> 22.5, 0.7 deg -> 0.9, 7 deg -> 9, 6 + 29 = 35 -> 36; H 'would be 22%' -> 23%, 22 months -> 23; I 3 1/2 slabs -> 4 1/2, 17 pieces -> 16, 'six give only 30' -> 31; K (315 keys) -> 316, 'keeps 35%' -> 36%. 5 were caught: H 0.65 -> 0.64 and 228 -> 227 aboard, I 54 -> 53 pieces, K 42% -> 43% and 5,802 -> 5,803.
3. The kinds year / cited / structural are never checked, so a computed number can sit under 'cited': G has 7 such rows (179.99 and six witness angles), K has 2 (22.5, 54.6). All 9 are right (recomputed), and the authors say so in the rows, but the tool cannot see a wrong one.
4. Most descriptions already tie each sentence to oracle keys in brackets ([F-D.h1.coverage], [K-P2.lone_pct.*]). Requiring each number to agree with a fact whose key is named in the same bullet or paragraph would close most of the gap in 1 and 2 (it would also have forced rows for 23/10/3%, 22%, 315 keys). Short of that, the pass line should read 'present in the oracle', and a reading of the text against the oracle (as the H audit did) remains the real check.

comments.author: GrayCave
comments.text:
GrayCave, tag-binding LANDED in de97ece (tools/description_numbers.py, tools/test_description_numbers.py 57 tests, tools/facts_check.py summary, tools/test_facts_check.py, descriptions + allow-lists of G, H, I, J, K on top of the step-2 commits 75b8be1, 213cb57, b7aa6d8, f7e51f8; E's tsv gets the legacy line, F has it from 2915e23; G fact sheet row 13_6 no longer lists the counts nobody reproduced).

RULE. The text is read in units (a list item with its continuation lines, a paragraph, a heading, a table, a code block). A unit that names fact keys ([K-T5.forces_kn], `F-C.mvl.*`, [K-B1.twist_per_min, .twist_hz], a range a.k1..k4) is bound to them: every number in it must agree (rounded as the text likes, never truncated or changed) with a number of THOSE keys, or have an allow-list row. A number in a unit that names no key needs a row however many facts it equals. Limit: the binding is to the UNION of the unit's keys, so a wrong small number that equals another number of a key tagged in the same unit still passes (a 36% beside a tagged 36.2 was one; K's economy paragraph is split for it, I's circle bullet likewise).

FORMULA DIGITS (the only numbers not checked against facts), exactly: 0 and 1; and a whole number under 100, no point, no percent, that is (a) a coefficient or exponent: a letter attached (2k, 3x), a superscript or ^ after or before it (x^2, 3^k); (b) beside an operator + - x / * ^ sqrt, only when the expression it belongs to (the run of digits, operators and brackets, plus one-letter variables joined by an operator or bracket, plus superscripts and roots) contains a variable, a superscript or a root: 2k + 1, n(n + 1)/2, 1 + 3 + ... + (2n - 1), (1, 1, 0)/sqrt(2); (c) the argument of a name, SE(3) or f(2), or a number that labels a vector, 2 (0, 1, 0). NOT exempt: a term of a sum of plain numbers (6 + 29 = 35, 3-4-5, 7 by 7), a hyphen after a letter (MTNS-83), k = 62, every decimal or percent, every number from 100 up. So a computed value written inside a formula is checked: a wrong entry of e^A in a matrix (J), a wrong decay rate in e^{-0.2t}, a wrong 2 x 212.2 = 424.4 (K) all FAIL (planted in the tests). Complete sums in the text are evaluated (6 + 29 = 36 fails). Also not read: HTML comments, fact keys, beat ids, chapter/joint/axis/row/column/table/figure N, section marks, volume(issue) locators, timestamps, ISO dates, list markers and a bold chapter label, URLs, Sources headings.

PLANTED ERRORS (17 off-by-one cases of the audit, G 5, H 4, I 4, K 4, written into the real tagged descriptions): old tool 5 of 17 caught, new tool 17 of 17. They are also tests (57 tests; the 17, four formula-hiding plants, a legacy file that passes under the old rule and fails without the line).

OFF-BY-ONE SWEEP (every number of each description, +1 and -1 in its last place, one at a time; my own sweep script, EmeraldOwl's was not in reach). Share caught of the numbers the tool checks by design (formula digits and unread tokens excluded), old tool on the descriptions before step 2 -> new tool on the landed ones: G 53% -> 92%, H 44% -> 89%, I 21% -> 71%, J 38% -> 85%, K 51% -> 85%; E 41% -> 48% and F 47% -> 52% (both still legacy, so they only gain from the conversion of their derived rows). Share of ALL changes caught: G 38 -> 49%, H 36 -> 66%, I 20 -> 48%, J 28 -> 48%, K 45 -> 62%, E 28 -> 27%, F 42 -> 45%. Of the 352 changes the tool still misses among the checked numbers of G-K, 338 (96%) are the union limit (a small whole number that becomes another number of a key tagged in the same unit), 9 turn into a formula digit by the change (su(3) to su(2)), 5 are other (2 in a G table row, 2 in I, 1 in J). The sweep script is not committed.

FACT KEY PATTERN. The old pattern missed two-character families (K-T5, G-X6, F-DO, K-B2), so those tags were never checked for existence and their digits were read as numbers; both fixed. A bracket may now wrap a line break ([K-R1.error_percent,\n.error_bound_percent]).

LEGACY. E (fair_coin: 98 numbers untagged under the strict rule) and F (mental_math) carry '#! legacy'; the summary line of a legacy video starts 'LEGACY (not tag-bound)' in tools/description_numbers.py and in the facts-check line. This bead closes only when git grep '^#! legacy' over the description_numbers.tsv files is empty; GoldenMountain is tagging E and F.

NOT DONE / OPEN. (1) J still passes with derived rows (3125, 1957, 1,920, 160,000, 354) until GoldenMountain's matrix_exponential oracle rows exist; then J's rows go and its bullets are tagged. (2) Spelled-out numbers are still not read. comments.author: GrayCave
comments.text:
GrayCave, 92d8de1 fixes the two bugs EmeraldOwl found in de97ece and adds the identity check GreenCarp asked about. 64 tests (tools/test_description_numbers.py), tools/test_facts_check.py 6; all seven videos pass at HEAD with fresh oracles (G, H, I, J, K tag-bound; E and F as the tsv files at HEAD say).

(1) A UNIT LETTER WAS READ AS A VARIABLE (K:197 'A box 45 x 23 x 18 m is 18,630 m3'). Cause: a letter a space after a number counted as a variable and the m3 superscript as another, so the expression was a formula and 45, 23, 18 were never checked. Now a letter a space after a number is a variable only when it is used like one (50 e^{-0.2t}, 3 x (y + 1), 2 n + 1: the next thing is ^, an operator or a bracket); glued to the digit (2k) or after an operator it still is. Plants on the real K text: 45 -> 46, 23 -> 24, 18 m -> 19 m each FAIL (the dimensions are bound to their fact now; the product is not evaluated, each dimension is checked). The change exposed exactly one number in the corpus: the 2 of the round trip in '343 / (2 x 2.5 m) = 68.6 Hz', a structural row in K's allow-list. Tests: FormulaDigits.test_a_unit_after_a_number_is_not_a_variable, UnitDimensions.

(2) A SUM AFTER 'N,' WAS NEVER EVALUATED (F:101 '23 x 46, (2 + 3) x (4 + 6) - 8 - 18 = 24'). Cause: the left scan took '46,' into the expression and then skipped it as implicit multiplication; a second guard skipped any expression that follows a comma. A comma followed by a space now ends the expression (a thousands comma has no space). Plant on the real F text: '= 25' FAILS ('does not come out, the left side is 24'). Test: Sums.test_a_comma_and_a_space_end_the_expression_on_the_left.

(3) IDENTITIES WITH LETTERS. Yes, an equation like '(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2' can be checked: both sides are parsed by a small algebra grammar (digits, single-letter symbols with subscripts, + - x / and implicit multiplication, powers, brackets, plus-or-minus tried with both signs) and evaluated exactly (Fractions) at six fixed points. It does not flood because it reports ONLY an equation that is no identity but would be with one number or one sign changed ('3 to 2'; '+ to -'; the candidates for a number are +-1, double, half, x10, /10 and 0..10): that is what a typo in an identity looks like, and a conditional equation (p^4 = 4p^3(1 - p) 'exactly when p = 4(1 - p)'), a definition (x = ...), a relation (a^2 + b^2 = c^2) or a law with words has no such neighbour. Not read at all, and so left alone: functions (sin, exp, log), sums, ellipses (a side next to one is cut), a letter glued to a digit, words, tags, matrices in brackets, a bare symbol or a number on either side. It computes in commuting scalars, so a matrix identity that holds only for commuting matrices is not flagged (it is true in scalars too).
 On the seven descriptions: 26 equations are read, 14 are true identities (F's seven rules: (10n + 5)^2, a^2 = (a - b)(a + b) + b^2, (a + b)(c + d), (a / 2)(2b), n(r - e), (a + b)(a - b), (50 +- b)^2; I's (a + b)^2 and n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6; J's e^{A+B} = e^A e^B and A e^{tA} = e^{tA} A), 12 are no identity and nothing is close (the ODEs of J, K phi = w^2 M phi, E's p^4 = 4p^3(1 - p), T(q) = e^{..}), 0 are flagged. Plants, one wrong number or sign in each real identity: 10 of 10 fail (F: 26 for 25, 6 for 5, 2b^2, 2bd, (3b), 2 x n x e, a^2 + b^2, 10b; I: 3ab, / 7). The commit message says 9 of 10 and a sign: that is imprecise, the tenth plant was I's '/ 7', first hidden by the ellipsis before it, caught after the per-side cut.
 What it does NOT cover, said straight: EmeraldOwl's I:56 'n(n + 1) / 2 -> / 3', I:80, I:48, I:110, I:104, I:66 stand in prose with no equals sign, so there is nothing to compare them to; those stay as formula digits. A tag-binding for a formula's coefficients (not 0, 1, 2) would be a writing convention (a key for the formula), not a tool fix.

STILL OPEN from the review: (c) consistent-but-wrong sums (49 - 24 = 25 -> 49 - 25 = 24 where each operand is a number of the tagged key), (d) a mix-up between keys named in one bullet, (e) neighbours in one key's list, (f) small wholes that are other numbers of the bullet's keys: the union limit; sentence-level binding is the next increment. mx-zbp5 stays open until no '#! legacy' line is left.

Comparing B with D holds that embedding and the reference recording fixed. Comparing A with E or C with D changes both the speaker representation and reference conditioning.
